sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十六】 起旃蒙單閼，盡柔兆執徐，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 76] From Shamen Dan'e through Rouzhao Zhisi; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals 76] From Shamen Dan'e through Rouzhao Zhisi—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之下乾寧二年（

translations.literal: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial, Qianning year 2 (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial—Qianning year 2 (

sentences.zh: 乙卯，公元八九五年）

translations.literal: yimao, corresponding to 895 CE).
translations.idiomatic: yimao, corresponding to 895 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛酉，幽州軍民數萬以麾蓋歌鼓迎李克用入府捨；

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, on xinyou, tens of thousands of soldiers and civilians of Youzhou welcomed Li Keyong into the government residence with banners, canopies, songs, and drums;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on xinyou, tens of thousands of Youzhou troops and civilians welcomed Li Keyong into the government compound with banners, canopies, music, and drums;

sentences.zh: 克用命李存審、劉仁恭將兵略定巡屬。

translations.literal: Keyong ordered Li Cunshen and Liu Rengong to lead troops and pacify the surrounding districts.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong ordered Li Cunshen and Liu Rengong to lead troops and bring the surrounding districts under control.

sentences.zh: 癸未，朱全忠遣其將朱友恭圍兗州，朱瑄自鄆以兵糧救之，友恭設伏，敗之於高梧，盡奪其餉，擒河東將安福順、安福慶。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Zhu Quanzhong sent his general Zhu Yougong to besiege Yanzhou. Zhu Xuan came from Yan with troops and grain to relieve it. Yougong laid an ambush and defeated him at Gaowu, seized all his supplies, and captured the Hedong generals An Fushun and An Fuqing.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Zhu Quanzhong sent his general Zhu Yougong to besiege Yanzhou. Zhu Xuan marched from Yan with troops and provisions to relieve the city. Yougong set an ambush and routed him at Gaowu, seized all his supplies, and took captive the Hedong generals An Fushun and An Fuqing.

sentences.zh: 己已，以給事中陸希聲為戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On jisi, Lu Xisheng, a supervising secretary, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, Lu Xisheng, supervising secretary, was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 希聲，元方五世孫也。

translations.literal: Xisheng was a fifth-generation descendant of Lu Yuanfang.
translations.idiomatic: Xisheng was a fifth-generation descendant of Lu Yuanfang.

sentences.zh: 壬申，護國節度使王重盈薨，軍中請以重榮子行軍司馬珂知留後事。

translations.literal: On renshen, Wang Chongying, military governor of Huguo, died. The army requested that Ke, son of Chongrong and acting army marshal, be made acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Wang Chongying, military governor of Huguo, died. The army asked that Ke—Chongrong's son and acting army marshal—be appointed acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 珂，重盈兄重簡之子也，重榮養以為子。

translations.literal: Ke was the son of Chongying's elder brother Chongjian; Chongrong had adopted him as his son.
translations.idiomatic: Ke was the son of Chongying's elder brother Chongjian; Chongrong had adopted him as his own.

sentences.zh: 楊行密表朱全忠罪惡，請會易定、兗、鄆、河東兵討之。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi memorialized listing Zhu Quanzhong's crimes and requested that troops from Yiding, Yan, Yan, and Hedong join to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi submitted a memorial detailing Zhu Quanzhong's crimes and asking that forces from Yiding, Yan, Yan, and Hedong unite to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 董昌將稱帝，集將佐議之。

translations.literal: Dong Chang was about to declare himself emperor and gathered his generals and aides to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang was preparing to declare himself emperor and summoned his generals and staff to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 節度副使黃碣曰：「今唐室雖微，天人未厭。

translations.literal: The deputy military governor Huang Jie said, "Though the Tang house is now feeble, Heaven and men have not yet turned against it.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy military governor Huang Jie said, "The Tang house may be weak, but Heaven and the people have not yet abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 齊桓、晉文皆翼戴周室以成霸業。

translations.literal: Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin both supported the Zhou house to achieve hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin both upheld the Zhou house and thereby achieved hegemony.

sentences.zh: 大王興於畎畝，受朝廷厚恩，位至將相，富貴極矣，奈何一旦忽為族滅之計乎！

translations.literal: Your Highness rose from the fields, received great favor from the court, rose to the rank of general and minister, and attained the utmost wealth and honor—why suddenly contemplate a course that will exterminate your clan!
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness rose from humble origins, received great favor from the court, rose to general and minister, and reached the height of wealth and honor—why would you suddenly embrace a plan that will destroy your entire clan!

sentences.zh: 碣寧死為忠臣，不生為叛逆！」

translations.literal: Jie would rather die a loyal minister than live a rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: I would rather die a loyal minister than live as a rebel!"

sentences.zh: 昌怒，以為惑眾，斬之，投其首於廁中，罵之曰：「奴賊負我！

translations.literal: Chang flew into a rage, deemed him a demagogue, executed him, and threw his head into a privy, cursing, "Slave-traitor, you betrayed me!
translations.idiomatic: Chang was enraged, judged him guilty of misleading the masses, had him beheaded, and threw his head into a latrine, crying, "Slave-traitor, you betrayed me!

sentences.zh: 好聖明時三公不能待，而先求死也！」

translations.literal: In this enlightened age you could not wait to become one of the Three Dukes, yet rushed to seek death first!"
translations.idiomatic: In this enlightened age you could not wait to become one of the Three Dukes, yet you rushed to seek death first!"

sentences.zh: 並殺其家八十口，同坎瘞之。

translations.literal: He also killed eighty members of Huang's household and buried them together in one pit.
translations.idiomatic: He also executed eighty members of Huang's household and buried them together in a single pit.

sentences.zh: 又問會稽令吳鐐，對曰：「大王不為真諸侯以傳子孫，乃欲假天子以取滅亡邪！」

translations.literal: He next questioned the magistrate of Kuaiji, Wu Liao, who replied, "Your Highness could remain a true feudatory and pass your domain to your descendants—why would you borrow the title of Son of Heaven only to court destruction!"
translations.idiomatic: He next questioned the magistrate of Kuaiji, Wu Liao, who replied, "Your Highness could remain a true feudal lord and pass your domain to your descendants—why borrow the title of Son of Heaven only to court destruction!"

sentences.zh: 昌亦族誅之。

translations.literal: Chang also executed Wu and his entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Chang had Wu and his entire clan executed as well.

sentences.zh: 又謂山陰令張遜曰：「汝有能政，吾深知之，俟吾為帝，命汝知御史臺。」

translations.literal: He also said to the magistrate of Shanyin, Zhang Xun, "You have governed ably; I know this well. When I become emperor I shall appoint you to head the Censorate."
translations.idiomatic: He also told the magistrate of Shanyin, Zhang Xun, "You have governed ably, and I know it well. When I become emperor I shall appoint you to head the Censorate."

sentences.zh: 遜曰：「大王起石鏡鎮，建節浙東，榮貴近二十年，何苦效李錡、劉辟之所為乎！

translations.literal: Xun said, "Your Highness rose from Shijing town, received a commandery in eastern Zhe, and has enjoyed glory and wealth for nearly twenty years—why painfully imitate what Li Qi and Liu Pi did!
translations.idiomatic: Xun said, "Your Highness rose from Shijing town, received a commandery in eastern Zhe, and has enjoyed glory and wealth for nearly twenty years—why imitate the fates of Li Qi and Liu Pi!

sentences.zh: 浙東僻處海隅，巡屬雖有六州，大王若稱帝，彼必不從，徒守孤城，為天下笑耳！」

translations.literal: Eastern Zhe lies remote on the sea's edge. Though your circuit has six prefectures, if Your Highness declares himself emperor they will surely not follow; you would merely hold a lone city and become the laughingstock of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Zhe lies remote on the coast. Though your circuit has six prefectures, if you declare yourself emperor they will surely not follow; you would merely hold a lone city and become the laughingstock of the realm!"

sentences.zh: 昌又殺之，謂人曰：「無此三人者，則人莫我違矣！」

translations.literal: Chang killed him too and told others, "Without these three men, no one would dare oppose me!"
translations.idiomatic: Chang killed him as well and told others, "Without these three men, no one would dare oppose me!"

sentences.zh: 二月，辛卯，昌被兗冕登子城門樓，即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the second month, on xinmao, Chang donned the imperial regalia, ascended the gate tower of the inner city, and took the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on xinmao, Chang donned imperial regalia, ascended the inner city's gate tower, and proclaimed himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 悉陳瑞物於庭以示眾。

translations.literal: He displayed all auspicious objects in the courtyard to show the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: He displayed all auspicious objects in the courtyard for the assembled crowd to see.

sentences.zh: 先是，咸通末，吳、越間訛言山中有大鳥，四目三足，聲云「羅平天冊」，見者有殃，民間多畫像以祀之。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the end of the Xiantong era, a rumor spread between Wu and Yue that a great bird with four eyes and three feet dwelt in the mountains; its cry was said to be "Luoping, the heavenly mandate." Those who saw it met misfortune, and the people widely painted its image to worship it.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of the Xiantong era, rumor spread through Wu and Yue of a great bird in the mountains with four eyes and three feet, whose cry was said to be "Luoping, the heavenly mandate." Those who saw it met misfortune, and people widely painted its image for worship.

sentences.zh: 及昌僭號，曰：「此吾鸑鷟也。」

translations.literal: When Chang usurped the imperial title he said, "This is my yuèzhuó."
translations.idiomatic: When Chang usurped the imperial title he said, "This is my yuèzhuó bird."

sentences.zh: 乃自稱大越羅平國，改元順天，署城樓曰天冊之樓，令群下謂己曰：「聖人」。

translations.literal: He styled his state Great Yue Luoping, changed the era name to Shuntian, named the gate tower the Tower of the Heavenly Mandate, and ordered his followers to address him as "the Sage."
translations.idiomatic: He styled his state Great Yue Luoping, changed the era name to Shuntian, named the gate tower the Tower of the Heavenly Mandate, and ordered his followers to address him as "the Sage."

sentences.zh: 以前杭州刺史李邈、前婺州刺史蔣瑰、兩浙鹽鐵副使杜郢、前屯田郎中李瑜為相。

translations.literal: He appointed the former prefect of Hangzhou Li Miao, the former prefect of Wuzhou Jiang Gui, the deputy commissioner of the Two Zhes Salt and Iron Monopoly Du Ying, and the former director of the Directorate of Agriculture Li Yu as chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the former prefect of Hangzhou Li Miao, the former prefect of Wuzhou Jiang Gui, the deputy commissioner of the Two Zhes Salt and Iron Monopoly Du Ying, and the former director of the Directorate of Agriculture Li Yu as chancellors.

sentences.zh: 又以吳瑤等皆為翰林學士、李暢之等皆為大將軍。

translations.literal: He also made Wu Yao and others Hanlin academicians and Li Changzhi and others great generals.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Wu Yao and others Hanlin academicians and Li Changzhi and others great generals.

sentences.zh: 昌移書錢鏐，告以權即羅平國位，以鏐為兩浙都指揮使。

translations.literal: Chang sent a letter to Qian Liu informing him that he was provisionally assuming the throne of Luoping and appointing Liu commander-in-chief of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: Chang wrote to Qian Liu informing him that he was provisionally assuming the throne of Luoping and appointing Liu commander-in-chief of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 鏐遺昌書曰：「與其閉門作天子，與九族、百姓俱陷塗炭，豈若開門作節度使，終身富貴邪！

translations.literal: Liu sent Chang a letter saying, "Rather than shutting your gates to play Son of Heaven and plunging your nine clans and the common people into misery, would it not be better to open your gates and remain a military governor, wealthy and honored for life!
translations.idiomatic: Liu wrote back to Chang, "Rather than shutting your gates to play Son of Heaven and plunging your nine clans and the common people into misery, would it not be better to open your gates and remain a military governor, wealthy and honored for life!

sentences.zh: 及今悛悔，尚可及也！」

translations.literal: If you repent now, it is still not too late!"
translations.idiomatic: If you repent now, it is still not too late!"

sentences.zh: 昌不聽，鏐乃將兵三萬詣越州城下，至迎恩門見昌，再拜言曰：「大王位兼將相，奈何捨安就危！

translations.literal: Chang would not listen. Liu then led thirty thousand troops to the walls of Yuezhou, came to the Gate of Welcoming Grace to see Chang, bowed twice, and said, "Your Highness holds the rank of both general and minister—why abandon security for peril!
translations.idiomatic: Chang would not listen. Liu then led thirty thousand troops to Yuezhou, came to the Gate of Welcoming Grace to see Chang, bowed twice, and said, "Your Highness holds the rank of both general and minister—why abandon security for peril!

sentences.zh: 鏐將兵此來，以俟大王改過耳。

translations.literal: I have brought troops here only to await Your Highness's reform.
translations.idiomatic: I have brought troops here only to await Your Highness's reform.

sentences.zh: 若天子命將出師，縱大王不自惜，鄉里士民何罪，隨大王族滅乎！」

translations.literal: If the Son of Heaven orders a general to march, even if Your Highness does not value your own life, what crime have the gentry and common people of this region committed that they should be exterminated with you!"
translations.idiomatic: If the Son of Heaven orders a general to march, even if Your Highness does not value your own life, what crime have the gentry and common people of this region committed that they should be exterminated with you!"

sentences.zh: 昌懼，致犒軍錢二百萬，執首謀者吳瑤及巫覡數人送於鏐，且請待罪天子。

translations.literal: Chang was afraid. He sent two million in cash to reward the army, seized the chief plotter Wu Yao and several shamans and delivered them to Liu, and asked to await judgment from the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was frightened. He sent two million in cash to reward the army, seized the chief plotter Wu Yao and several shamans and delivered them to Liu, and asked to await judgment from the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 鏐引兵還，以狀聞。

translations.literal: Liu withdrew his troops and reported the matter to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Liu withdrew his troops and reported the matter to the court.

sentences.zh: 王重盈之子保義節度使珙、晉州刺史瑤舉兵擊王珂，表言珂非王氏子。

translations.literal: Wang Chongying's sons—Wang Gong, military governor of Baoyi, and Wang Yao, prefect of Jin—raised troops to attack Wang Ke and memorialized that Ke was not a son of the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongying's sons—Wang Gong, military governor of Baoyi, and Wang Yao, prefect of Jin—raised troops to attack Wang Ke and memorialized that Ke was not a son of the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 與朱全忠書，言「珂本吾家蒼頭，不應為嗣。」

translations.literal: They wrote to Zhu Quanzhong, saying, "Ke was originally a household slave of our family and ought not to succeed."
translations.idiomatic: They wrote to Zhu Quanzhong, saying, "Ke was originally a household slave in our family and ought not to succeed."

sentences.zh: 珂上表自陳，且求援於李克用。

translations.literal: Ke submitted a memorial in his own defense and also sought aid from Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Ke submitted a memorial in his own defense and also sought aid from Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使諭解之。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct them to stand down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to instruct them to stand down.

sentences.zh: 上重李谿文學，乙未，復以谿為戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Li Xi's literary talent. On yiwei he again appointed Xi Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Li Xi's literary talent. On yiwei he again appointed Xi Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 己酉，朱全忠軍於單父，為朱友恭聲援。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Zhu Quanzhong encamped at Shanfu to support Zhu Yougong.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Zhu Quanzhong encamped at Shanfu to support Zhu Yougong.

sentences.zh: 李克用表劉仁恭為盧龍留後，留兵戍之；

translations.literal: Li Keyong memorialized requesting Liu Rengong as acting military governor of Lulong and left troops to garrison the region;
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong memorialized requesting Liu Rengong as acting military governor of Lulong and left troops to garrison the region;

sentences.zh: 壬子，還晉陽。

translations.literal: on renzi he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: on renzi he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 媯州人高思繼兄弟，在武干，為燕人所服，克用皆以為都將，分掌幽州兵；

translations.literal: The brothers Gao Siji of Guizhou, skilled in arms and respected by the people of Yan, Keyong all appointed as commanders and divided control of the Youzhou troops among them;
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Gao Siji of Guizhou, skilled in arms and respected by the people of Yan—Keyong appointed them all as commanders and divided control of the Youzhou troops among them;

sentences.zh: 部下士卒，皆山北之豪也，仁恭憚之。

translations.literal: the soldiers under their command were all powerful men of the northern mountains, and Rengong feared them.
translations.idiomatic: their soldiers were all powerful men of the northern mountains, and Rengong feared them.

sentences.zh: 久之，河東兵戍幽州者暴橫，思繼兄弟以法裁之，所誅殺甚多。

translations.literal: After a time the Hedong troops garrisoning Youzhou grew violent and overbearing; the Gao brothers punished them by law and executed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: After a time the Hedong troops garrisoning Youzhou grew violent and overbearing; the Gao brothers punished them by law and executed a great many.

sentences.zh: 克用怒，以讓仁恭，仁恭訴稱高氏兄弟所為，克用俱殺之。

translations.literal: Keyong was angry and reproached Rengong. Rengong pleaded that the Gao brothers were responsible, and Keyong had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was angry and reproached Rengong. Rengong pleaded that the Gao brothers were responsible, and Keyong had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 仁恭欲收燕人心，復引其諸子置帳下，厚撫之。

translations.literal: Rengong wished to win the hearts of the people of Yan; he again took the Gao brothers' sons into his retinue and treated them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Rengong wished to win the hearts of the people of Yan; he again took the Gao brothers' sons into his retinue and treated them generously.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯與李茂貞、王行瑜深相結，得天子過失，朝廷機事，悉以告之。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei was deeply allied with Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu; whenever he learned of the Son of Heaven's faults or confidential court affairs, he reported them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei was deeply allied with Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu; whenever he learned of the emperor's faults or confidential court affairs, he reported them all.

sentences.zh: 邠寧節度副使崔鋋，昭緯之族也，李谿再入相，昭緯使鋋告行瑜曰：「向者尚書令之命已行矣，而韋昭度沮之，今又引李谿為同列，相與熒惑聖聽，恐復有杜太尉之事。」

translations.literal: Cui Chan, deputy military governor of Binning and a kinsman of Zhaowei—when Li Xi reentered the chancellery, Zhaowei had Chan tell Xingyu, "Earlier the appointment as Director of the Department of State Affairs had already been issued, yet Wei Zhaodu blocked it. Now they have brought Li Xi in as a colleague; together they bewilder the imperial ear—I fear there will again be an affair like that of Duke Du."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Chan, deputy military governor of Binning and a kinsman of Zhaowei—when Li Xi reentered the chancellery, Zhaowei had Chan tell Xingyu, "Earlier the appointment as Director of the Department of State Affairs had already been issued, yet Wei Zhaodu blocked it. Now they have brought Li Xi in as a colleague; together they bewilder the imperial ear—I fear there will again be an affair like that of Duke Du."

sentences.zh: 行瑜乃與茂貞表稱谿奸邪，昭度無相業，宜罷居散秩。

translations.literal: Xingyu then joined Maozhen in a memorial calling Xi treacherous and wicked and saying Zhaodu lacked the capacity of a chancellor; both should be dismissed to honorary posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu then joined Maozhen in a memorial calling Xi treacherous and wicked and saying Zhaodu lacked the capacity of a chancellor; both should be dismissed to honorary posts.

sentences.zh: 上報曰：「軍旅之事，聯則與籓鎮圖之；

translations.literal: The emperor replied, "On military affairs I shall consult with the frontier commands;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied, "On military affairs I shall consult with the frontier commands;

sentences.zh: 至於命相，當出朕懷。」

translations.literal: as for appointing chancellors, that must come from my own mind."
translations.idiomatic: as for appointing chancellors, that must come from my own mind."

sentences.zh: 行瑜等論列不已，三月，谿復罷為太子少師。

translations.literal: Xingyu and the others argued on without cease. In the third month Xi was again dismissed and made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu and the others argued on without cease. In the third month Xi was again dismissed and made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 王珙、王瑤請朝廷命河中帥，詔以中書侍郎、同平章事崔胤同平章事，充護國節度使；

translations.literal: Wang Gong and Wang Yao asked the court to appoint a military governor of Hezhong. An edict made Cui Yin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Chancellery, also Director of the Chancellery and military governor of Huguo;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong and Wang Yao asked the court to appoint a military governor of Hezhong. An edict made Cui Yin, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Chancellery, military governor of Huguo as well;

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎、判戶部王摶為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: and appointed Wang Tuan, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting head of the ministry, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Wang Tuan, Vice Minister of Revenue and acting head of the ministry, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 王珂，李克用之婿也。

translations.literal: Wang Ke was Li Keyong's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke was Li Keyong's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 克用表重榮有功於國，請賜其子珂節鉞。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized that Chongrong had rendered great service to the state and requested that his son Ke be granted the command.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong memorialized that Chongrong had rendered great service to the state and requested that his son Ke be granted the command.

sentences.zh: 王珙厚結王行瑜、李茂貞、韓建三帥，更上表稱珂非王氏子，請以珂為陝州、珙為河中。

translations.literal: Wang Gong cultivated close ties with the three commanders Wang Xingyu, Li Maozhen, and Han Jian and again memorialized that Ke was not a Wang clansman, requesting that Ke be given Shaan and Gong be given Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gong cultivated close ties with the three commanders Wang Xingyu, Li Maozhen, and Han Jian and again memorialized that Ke was not a Wang clansman, requesting that Ke be given Shaan and Gong be given Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 上諭以先已允克用之秦，不許。

translations.literal: The emperor explained that he had already granted Keyong's request and would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor explained that he had already granted Keyong's request and would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 加王鎔兼侍中。

translations.literal: Wang Rong was additionally appointed Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong was additionally appointed Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 楊行密浮淮至泗州，防禦使台濛盛飾供帳，行密不悅。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sailed the Huai to Sizhou. The defense commissioner Tai Meng lavishly prepared his reception quarters, and Xingmi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sailed the Huai to Sizhou. Defense commissioner Tai Meng lavishly prepared his reception quarters, and Xingmi was displeased.

sentences.zh: 既行，濛於臥內得補綻衣，馳使歸之。

translations.literal: After he had departed, Meng found a patched garment in the sleeping quarters and sent a courier at full speed to return it.
translations.idiomatic: After he had departed, Meng found a patched garment in the sleeping quarters and sent a courier at full speed to return it.

sentences.zh: 行密笑曰：「吾少貧賤，不敢忘本。」

translations.literal: Xingmi laughed and said, "In my youth I was poor and lowly; I dare not forget my origins."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi laughed and said, "In my youth I was poor and lowly; I dare not forget my origins."

sentences.zh: 濛甚慚。

translations.literal: Meng was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 行密攻濠州，撥之，執刺史張璲。

translations.literal: Xingmi attacked Haozhou, captured it, and seized the prefect Zhang Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi attacked Haozhou, captured it, and seized the prefect Zhang Jin.

sentences.zh: 行密軍士掠得徐州人李氏之子，生八年矣，行密養以為子，行密長子渥憎之；

translations.literal: Xingmi's soldiers had plundered a son of the Li clan of Xuzhou, eight years old; Xingmi adopted him as a son, but Xingmi's eldest son Wo hated him;
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi's soldiers had plundered a son of the Li clan of Xuzhou, eight years old; Xingmi adopted him as a son, but Xingmi's eldest son Wo hated him;

sentences.zh: 行密謂其將徐溫曰：「此兒質狀性識，頗異於人，吾度渥必不能容，今賜汝為子。」

translations.literal: Xingmi said to his general Xu Wen, "This boy's appearance and nature are quite unlike others. I reckon Wo will surely not tolerate him; I now give him to you as a son."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi said to his general Xu Wen, "This boy's appearance and nature are quite unlike others. I reckon Wo will surely not tolerate him; I now give him to you as a son."

sentences.zh: 溫名之曰知誥。

translations.literal: Wen named him Zhigao.
translations.idiomatic: Wen named him Zhigao.

sentences.zh: 知誥事溫，勤孝過於諸子。

translations.literal: Zhigao served Wen with diligence and filial piety surpassing Wen's other sons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao served Wen with diligence and filial piety surpassing Wen's other sons.

sentences.zh: 嘗得罪於溫，溫笞而逐之；

translations.literal: Once he offended Wen; Wen flogged him and drove him out;
translations.idiomatic: Once he offended Wen; Wen flogged him and drove him out;

sentences.zh: 及歸，知誥迎拜於門。

translations.literal: when Wen returned, Zhigao met him at the gate with bows.
translations.idiomatic: when Wen returned, Zhigao met him at the gate with bows.

sentences.zh: 溫問：「何故猶在此？」

translations.literal: Wen asked, "Why are you still here?"
translations.idiomatic: Wen asked, "Why are you still here?"

sentences.zh: 知誥泣對曰：「人子捨父母將何之！

translations.literal: Zhigao wept and replied, "Where would a son go if he abandoned his parents!
translations.idiomatic: Zhigao wept and replied, "Where would a son go if he abandoned his parents!

sentences.zh: 父怒而歸母，人情之常也。」

translations.literal: When a father is angry a son returns to his mother—that is human nature."
translations.idiomatic: When a father is angry a son returns to his mother—that is human nature."

sentences.zh: 溫以是益愛之，使掌家事，家人無違言。

translations.literal: Wen therefore loved him all the more, put him in charge of household affairs, and the family offered no dissent.
translations.idiomatic: Wen therefore loved him all the more, put him in charge of household affairs, and the family offered no dissent.

sentences.zh: 及長，喜書善射，識度英偉。

translations.literal: When he grew up he loved books and was skilled at archery, with lofty insight and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he loved books and was skilled at archery, with lofty insight and bearing.

sentences.zh: 行密常謂溫曰：「知誥俊傑，諸將子皆不及也。」

translations.literal: Xingmi often told Wen, "Zhigao is a prodigy; none of the generals' sons can match him."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi often told Wen, "Zhigao is a prodigy; none of the generals' sons can match him."

sentences.zh: 丁亥，行密圍壽州。

translations.literal: On dinghai Xingmi besieged Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai Xingmi besieged Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 上以郊畿多盜，至有逾垣入宮或侵犯陵寢者，欲令宗室諸王將兵巡警，又欲使之四方撫慰籓鎮。

translations.literal: Because bandits were numerous in the capital suburbs—some even scaling walls to enter the palace or violating imperial tombs—the emperor wished to have princes of the imperial clan lead troops on patrol and also send them to comfort the frontier commands in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Because bandits were numerous in the capital suburbs—some even scaling walls to enter the palace or violating imperial tombs—the emperor wished to have princes of the imperial clan lead troops on patrol and also send them to comfort the frontier commands in all directions.

sentences.zh: 南北司用事之臣恐其不利於己，交章論諫。

translations.literal: The officials in power in the Northern and Southern Bureaus feared this would harm their interests and submitted memorial after memorial in opposition.
translations.idiomatic: The officials in power in the Northern and Southern Bureaus feared this would harm their interests and submitted memorial after memorial in opposition.

sentences.zh: 上不得已，夏，四月，下詔悉罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor had no choice. In summer, the fourth month, he issued an edict abolishing the plan entirely.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had no choice. In summer, the fourth month, he issued an edict abolishing the plan entirely.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以董昌有貢輸之勤，今日所為，類得心疾，詔釋其罪，縱歸田裡。

translations.literal: The court, considering that Dong Chang had long rendered tribute and that his present conduct resembled madness, issued an edict pardoning his crimes and allowing him to return to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: The court, considering that Dong Chang had long rendered tribute and that his present conduct resembled madness, issued an edict pardoning his crimes and allowing him to return to his fields.

sentences.zh: 戶部侍郎、同平章事陸希聲罷為太子少師。

translations.literal: Lu Xisheng, Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery, was dismissed and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xisheng, Vice Minister of Revenue and Director of the Chancellery, was dismissed and made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 楊行密圍壽州，不克，將還；

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi besieged Shouzhou but could not take it and was about to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi besieged Shouzhou but could not take it and was about to withdraw;

sentences.zh: 庚寅，其將朱延壽請試往更攻，一鼓撥之，執剌史江從勖。

translations.literal: on gengyin his general Zhu Yanshou asked to try another assault, took the city at the first drum, and seized the prefect Jiang Congxu.
translations.idiomatic: on gengyin his general Zhu Yanshou asked to try another assault, took the city at the first drum, and seized the prefect Jiang Congxu.

sentences.zh: 行密以延壽權知壽州團練使。

translations.literal: Xingmi made Yanshou acting military training commissioner of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi made Yanshou acting military training commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，汴兵數萬攻壽州，州中兵少，吏民忷懼。

translations.literal: Before long tens of thousands of Bian troops attacked Shouzhou. The garrison was small and officials and people were alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long tens of thousands of Bian troops attacked Shouzhou. The garrison was small and officials and people were alarmed.

sentences.zh: 延壽制，軍中每旗二十五騎。

translations.literal: Yanshou decreed that each banner in the army would have twenty-five horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou decreed that each banner in the army would have twenty-five horsemen.

sentences.zh: 命黑雲隊長李厚將十旗擊汴兵，不勝；

translations.literal: He ordered Li Hou, captain of the Black Cloud unit, to lead ten banners against the Bian troops; they did not prevail;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Li Hou, captain of the Black Cloud unit, to lead ten banners against the Bian troops; they did not prevail;

sentences.zh: 延壽將斬之，厚稱眾寡不敵，願益兵更往，不勝則死。

translations.literal: Yanshou was about to execute him. Hou pleaded that they were outnumbered, asked for more troops to try again, and said if he failed he would accept death.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou was about to execute him. Hou pleaded that they were outnumbered, asked for more troops to try again, and said if he failed he would accept death.

sentences.zh: 都押牙汝陽柴再用亦為之請，乃益以五旗。

translations.literal: Chai Zaiyong of Ruyang, chief military adjutant, also pleaded for him, and five more banners were added.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Zaiyong of Ruyang, chief military adjutant, also pleaded for him, and five more banners were added.

sentences.zh: 厚殊死戰，再用助之，延壽悉眾乘之，汴兵敗走。

translations.literal: Hou fought to the death, Zaiyong aided him, and Yanshou led the whole force in pursuit; the Bian troops were defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hou fought to the death, Zaiyong aided him, and Yanshou led the whole force in pursuit; the Bian troops were defeated and fled.

sentences.zh: 厚，蔡州人也。

translations.literal: Hou was a native of Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou was a native of Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 行密又遣兵襲漣水，撥之。

translations.literal: Xingmi also sent troops to raid Lianshui and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi also sent troops to raid Lianshui and captured it.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐表董昌僭逆，不可赦，請以本道兵討之。

translations.literal: Qian Liu memorialized that Dong Chang's usurpation could not be pardoned and requested permission to campaign against him with his circuit's troops.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu memorialized that Dong Chang's usurpation could not be pardoned and asked to campaign against him with his own circuit's troops.

sentences.zh: 太傅、門下侍郎、同平章事韋昭度以太保致仕。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery Wei Zhaodu retired as Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery Wei Zhaodu retired as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，以劉建鋒為武安節度使。

translations.literal: On wuxu Liu Jianfeng was appointed military governor of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Liu Jianfeng was appointed military governor of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 建鋒以馬殷為內外馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Jianfeng appointed Ma Yin commander-in-chief of all internal and external horse and foot forces.
translations.idiomatic: Jianfeng appointed Ma Yin commander-in-chief of all internal and external horse and foot forces.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣使詣錢鏐，言董昌已改過，宜釋之；

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent envoys to Qian Liu saying Dong Chang had reformed and should be pardoned;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent envoys to Qian Liu saying Dong Chang had reformed and should be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 亦遣詣昌，使趣朝貢。

translations.literal: he also sent envoys to Chang urging him to hurry with court tribute.
translations.idiomatic: he also sent envoys to Chang urging him to hurry with court tribute.

sentences.zh: 河東遣其將史儼、李承嗣以萬騎馳入於鄆，朱友恭退歸於汴。

translations.literal: Hedong sent its generals Shi Yan and Li Chengsi with ten thousand horsemen galloping into Yan; Zhu Yougong withdrew to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong sent its generals Shi Yan and Li Chengsi with ten thousand horsemen galloping into Yan; Zhu Yougong withdrew to Bian.

sentences.zh: 五月，詔削董昌官爵，委錢鏐討之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month an edict stripped Dong Chang of rank and title and entrusted Qian Liu with campaigning against him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month an edict stripped Dong Chang of rank and title and entrusted Qian Liu with campaigning against him.

sentences.zh: 初，王行瑜求尚書令不獲，由是怨朝廷。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Xingyu had sought the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs without success and therefore resented the court.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Xingyu had sought the post of Director of the Department of State Affairs without success and therefore resented the court.

sentences.zh: 畿內有八鎮兵，隸左右軍。

translations.literal: Within the capital region there were eight garrison commands, subordinate to the Left and Right Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital region there were eight garrison commands, subordinate to the Left and Right Armies.

sentences.zh: 郃陽鎮近華州，韓建求之；

translations.literal: Heyang Garrison lay near Hua, and Han Jian requested it;
translations.idiomatic: Heyang Garrison lay near Hua, and Han Jian requested it;

sentences.zh: 良原鎮近邠州，王行瑜求之。

translations.literal: Liangyuan Garrison lay near Bin, and Wang Xingyu requested it.
translations.idiomatic: Liangyuan Garrison lay near Bin, and Wang Xingyu requested it.

sentences.zh: 宦官曰：「此天子禁軍，何可得也！」

translations.literal: The eunuchs said, "These are the Son of Heaven's imperial guards—how can they be given away!"
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs said, "These are the Son of Heaven's imperial guards—how can they be given away!"

sentences.zh: 王珂、王珙爭河中，行瑜、建及李茂貞皆為珙請，不能得，恥之。

translations.literal: Wang Ke and Wang Gong contended for Hezhong. Xingyu, Jian, and Li Maozhen all pleaded Gong's case but could not obtain it and felt shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke and Wang Gong contended for Hezhong. Xingyu, Jian, and Li Maozhen all pleaded Gong's case but could not obtain it and felt humiliated.

sentences.zh: 珙使人語三帥曰：「珂不受代而與河東昏姻，必為諸公不利，請討之。」

translations.literal: Gong sent someone to tell the three commanders, "Ke refuses to step down and has married into Hedong—he will surely harm you all. Please campaign against him."
translations.idiomatic: Gong sent someone to tell the three commanders, "Ke refuses to step down and has married into Hedong—he will surely harm you all. Please campaign against him."

sentences.zh: 行瑜使其弟匡國節度使行約攻河中，珂求救於李克用。

translations.literal: Xingyu sent his younger brother Xingyue, military governor of Kuangguo, to attack Hezhong, and Ke sought rescue from Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu sent his younger brother Xingyue, military governor of Kuangguo, to attack Hezhong, and Ke sought rescue from Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 行瑜乃與茂貞、建各將精兵數千入朝，甲子，至京師，坊市民皆竄匿。

translations.literal: Xingyu then joined Maozhen and Jian, each leading several thousand elite troops into court. On jiazi they reached the capital; people in the wards and markets all fled and hid.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu then joined Maozhen and Jian, each leading several thousand elite troops to the capital. On jiazi they reached the city; people in the wards and markets all fled and hid.

sentences.zh: 上御安福門以待之，三帥盛陳甲兵，拜伏舞蹈於門下。

translations.literal: The emperor waited at the Gate of Peace and Fortune to receive them. The three commanders displayed their armor in full array and prostrated themselves dancing below the gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor waited at the Gate of Peace and Fortune to receive them. The three commanders paraded in full armor and prostrated themselves dancing below the gate.

sentences.zh: 上臨軒，親詰之曰：「卿輩不奏請俟報，輒稱兵入京城，其志欲何為乎？

translations.literal: The emperor came to the pavilion and questioned them in person: "You did not memorialize and await reply, yet raised troops and entered the capital—what do you intend?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to the pavilion and questioned them in person: "You did not memorialize and await reply, yet raised troops and entered the capital—what do you intend?

sentences.zh: 若不能事朕，今日請避賢路！」

translations.literal: If you cannot serve me, step aside today!"
translations.idiomatic: If you cannot serve me, step aside today!"

sentences.zh: 行瑜、茂貞流汗不能言，獨韓建粗述入朝之由。

translations.literal: Xingyu and Maozhen sweated and could not speak; only Han Jian roughly explained why they had come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu and Maozhen sweated and could not speak; only Han Jian roughly explained why they had come to court.

sentences.zh: 上與三帥宴，三帥奏稱：「南、北司互有朋黨，墮紊朝政。

translations.literal: The emperor dined with the three commanders. They reported, "The Northern and Southern Bureaus form factions with one another and corrupt government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dined with the three commanders. They reported, "The Northern and Southern Bureaus form factions with one another and corrupt government affairs.

sentences.zh: 韋昭度討西川失策，李谿作相，不合眾心，請誅之。」

translations.literal: Wei Zhaodu's western Sichuan campaign failed in strategy; Li Xi as chancellor does not suit popular sentiment—we ask that they be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu's western Sichuan campaign failed; Li Xi as chancellor does not suit popular sentiment—we ask that they be executed."

sentences.zh: 上未之許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not agree.

sentences.zh: 是日，行瑜等殺昭度、谿於都亭驛，又殺樞密使康尚弼及宦官數人。

translations.literal: That same day Xingyu and the others killed Zhaodu and Xi at the metropolitan courier station, and also killed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Kang Shangbi and several eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xingyu and the others killed Zhaodu and Xi at the metropolitan courier station, and also killed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Kang Shangbi and several eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 又言：「王珂、王珙嫡庶不分，請除王珙河中，徙王行約於陝，王珂於同州。」

translations.literal: They also said, "Wang Ke and Wang Gong do not distinguish legitimate from illegitimate succession—appoint Gong to Hezhong, move Wang Xingyue to Shaan, and Wang Ke to Tong."
translations.idiomatic: They also said, "Wang Ke and Wang Gong do not distinguish legitimate from illegitimate succession—appoint Gong to Hezhong, move Wang Xingyue to Shaan, and Wang Ke to Tong."

sentences.zh: 上皆許之。

translations.literal: The emperor granted all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted all.

sentences.zh: 始，三帥謀廢上，立吉王保；

translations.literal: At first the three commanders had plotted to depose the emperor and install Prince Bao of Ji;
translations.idiomatic: At first the three commanders had plotted to depose the emperor and install Prince Bao of Ji;

sentences.zh: 至是，聞李克用已起兵於河東，行瑜、茂貞各留兵二千人宿衛京師，與建皆辭還鎮。

translations.literal: by now they heard Li Keyong had raised troops in Hedong. Xingyu and Maozhen each left two thousand men to guard the capital, and all three took leave and returned to their commands.
translations.idiomatic: by now they heard Li Keyong had raised troops in Hedong. Xingyu and Maozhen each left two thousand men to guard the capital, and all three took leave and returned to their commands.

sentences.zh: 貶戶部尚書楊堪為雅州刺史。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Kan was demoted to prefect of Ya.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Revenue Yang Kan was demoted to prefect of Ya.

sentences.zh: 堪，虞卿之子，昭度之舅也。

translations.literal: Kan was the son of Yuqing and Zhaodu's maternal nephew.
translations.idiomatic: Kan was the son of Yuqing and Zhaodu's maternal nephew.

sentences.zh: 初，崔胤除河中節度使，河東進奏官薛志勤揚言曰：「崔公雖重德，以之代王珂，不若光德劉公於我公厚也。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Cui Yin was appointed military governor of Hezhong, Hedong's memorial envoy Xue Zhiqin proclaimed, "Though Lord Cui is greatly virtuous, replacing Wang Ke with him is not as good as Grandee Liu of Guangde, who is closer to our lord."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Cui Yin was appointed military governor of Hezhong, Hedong's memorial envoy Xue Zhiqin proclaimed, "Though Lord Cui is greatly virtuous, replacing Wang Ke with him is not as good as Grandee Liu of Guangde, who is closer to our lord."

sentences.zh: 光德劉公者，太常卿劉崇望也。

translations.literal: Grandee Liu of Guangde was Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Chongwang.
translations.idiomatic: Grandee Liu of Guangde was Grand Master of Ceremonies Liu Chongwang.

sentences.zh: 及三帥入朝，聞志勤之言，貶崇望昭州司馬。

translations.literal: When the three commanders entered court they heard Zhiqin's words and demoted Chongwang to military adjutant of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the three commanders entered court they heard Zhiqin's words and demoted Chongwang to military adjutant of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 李克用聞三鎮兵犯闕，即日遣使十三輩發北部兵，期以來月渡河入關。

translations.literal: Li Keyong heard the three circuits' troops had violated the capital and the same day sent thirteen envoys to mobilize northern troops, planning to cross the river and enter the passes the following month.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong heard the three circuits' troops had violated the capital and the same day sent thirteen envoys to mobilize northern troops, planning to cross the river and enter the passes the following month.

sentences.zh: 六月，庚寅，以錢鏐為浙東招討使；

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on gengyin, Qian Liu was made southeastern campaign commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on gengyin, Qian Liu was made southeastern campaign commissioner;

sentences.zh: 鏐復發兵擊董昌。

translations.literal: Liu again sent troops to attack Dong Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu again sent troops to attack Dong Chang.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，以前均州刺史孔緯、繡州司戶張濬並為太子賓客。

translations.literal: On xinmao the former prefect of Junzhou Kong Wei and the household registrar of Xiuzhou Zhang Jun were both made tutors of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the former prefect of Junzhou Kong Wei and the household registrar of Xiuzhou Zhang Jun were both made tutors of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，以緯為吏部尚書，復其階爵；

translations.literal: On renchen Wei was made Director of the Department of State Affairs and his rank and titles were restored;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Wei was made Director of the Department of State Affairs and his rank and titles were restored;

sentences.zh: 癸已，拜司空，兼門下侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: on guisi he was made Minister of Works, also Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: on guisi he was made Minister of Works, also Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 以張濬為兵部尚書、諸道租庸使。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and commissioner for all circuits' tax and corvée.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was made Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs and commissioner for all circuits' tax and corvée.

sentences.zh: 時緯居華州，濬居長水，上以崔昭緯等外交籓鎮，朋黨相傾，思得骨鯁之士，故驟用緯、濬。

translations.literal: At the time Wei lived at Hua and Zhang at Changshui. The emperor, seeing Cui Zhaowei and others dealing with frontier commands and factions overturning one another, wished for men of firm backbone and therefore suddenly elevated Wei and Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei lived at Hua and Zhang at Changshui. The emperor, seeing Cui Zhaowei and others dealing with frontier commands and factions overturning one another, wished for men of firm backbone and therefore suddenly elevated Wei and Zhang.

sentences.zh: 緯以有疾，扶輿至京師，見上，涕泣固辭；

translations.literal: Wei, being ill, was carried in a litter to the capital. Seeing the emperor he wept and firmly declined;
translations.idiomatic: Wei, being ill, was carried in a litter to the capital. Seeing the emperor he wept and firmly declined;

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: the emperor would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 李克用大舉蕃、漢兵南下，上表稱王行瑜、李茂貞、韓建稱兵犯闕，賊害大臣，請討之，又移檄三鎮，行瑜等大懼。

translations.literal: Li Keyong launched a great southern march of Tatar and Chinese troops. He memorialized that Wang Xingyu, Li Maozhen, and Han Jian had raised troops against the capital and murdered great ministers, requesting permission to campaign, and also sent proclamations to the three circuits. Xingyu and the others were greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong launched a great southern march of Tatar and Chinese troops. He memorialized that Wang Xingyu, Li Maozhen, and Han Jian had raised troops against the capital and murdered great ministers, requesting permission to campaign, and also sent proclamations to the three circuits. Xingyu and the others were greatly afraid.

sentences.zh: 克用軍至絳州，刺史王瑤閉城拒之；

translations.literal: Keyong's army reached Jiang Prefecture; the prefect Wang Yao closed the gates and resisted;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong's army reached Jiang Prefecture; the prefect Wang Yao closed the gates and resisted;

sentences.zh: 克用進攻，旬日，拔之。

translations.literal: Keyong pressed the assault; in ten days he took it.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong pressed the assault; in ten days he took it.

sentences.zh: 斬瑤於軍門，殺城中違拒者千餘人。

translations.literal: He executed Yao at the army gate and killed more than a thousand in the city who had defied him.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Yao at the army gate and killed more than a thousand in the city who had defied him.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙辰朔，克用至河中，王珂迎謁於路。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day bingchen of the month, Keyong reached Hezhong and Ke met and welcomed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the first day bingchen of the month, Keyong reached Hezhong and Ke met and welcomed him on the road.

sentences.zh: 匡國節度使王行約敗於朝邑，戊午，行約棄同州走，己未，至京師。

translations.literal: Kuangguo military governor Wang Xingyue was defeated at Chaoyi. On wuwu he abandoned Tong and fled; on jiwei he reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Kuangguo military governor Wang Xingyue was defeated at Chaoyi. On wuwu he abandoned Tong and fled; on jiwei he reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 行約弟行實時為左軍指揮使，帥眾與行約大掠西市。

translations.literal: Xingyue's younger brother Xingshi was then commander of the Left Army; he led troops with Xingyue to plunder the western market on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyue's younger brother Xingshi was then commander of the Left Army; he led troops with Xingyue to plunder the western market on a great scale.

sentences.zh: 行實奏稱同華已沒，沙陀將至，請車駕幸邠州。

translations.literal: Xingshi memorialized that Tong and Hua had fallen and the Shatuo were coming, requesting that the imperial carriage proceed to Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshi memorialized that Tong and Hua had fallen and the Shatuo were coming, requesting that the imperial carriage proceed to Bin.

sentences.zh: 庚申，樞密使駱全瓘奏請車駕幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: On gengshen Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Luo Quanjin memorialized requesting that the carriage proceed to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Luo Quanjin memorialized requesting that the carriage proceed to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「朕得克用表，尚駐軍河中。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "I have received Keyong's memorial; he is still encamped at Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have received Keyong's memorial; he is still encamped at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 就使沙陀至此，朕自有以枝梧，卿等但各撫本軍，勿令搖動。」

translations.literal: Even if the Shatuo arrive here, I have my own means to cope. Each of you only steady your own armies and do not let them stir."
translations.idiomatic: Even if the Shatuo arrive here, I have my own means to cope. Each of you only steady your own armies and do not let them stir."

sentences.zh: 右軍指揮使李繼鵬，茂貞假子也，本姓名閻珪，與駱全瓘謀劫上幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: Right Army commander Li Jipeng was Maozhen's adopted son, originally surnamed Yan Gui. He and Luo Quanjin plotted to seize the emperor for Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Right Army commander Li Jipeng was Maozhen's adopted son, originally surnamed Yan Gui. He and Luo Quanjin plotted to seize the emperor for Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 中尉劉景宣與王行實知之，欲劫上幸邠州。

translations.literal: Captain Liu Jingxuan and Wang Xingshi learned of it and wished to seize the emperor for Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Captain Liu Jingxuan and Wang Xingshi learned of it and wished to seize the emperor for Bin.

sentences.zh: 孔緯面折景宣，以為不可輕離宮闕。

translations.literal: Kong Wei rebuked Jingxuan to his face, saying they must not lightly leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei rebuked Jingxuan to his face, saying they must not lightly leave the palace.

sentences.zh: 向晚，繼鵬連奏請車駕出幸，於是王行約引左軍攻右軍，於樓前侍衛。

translations.literal: Toward evening Jipeng repeatedly memorialized asking the carriage to depart. Then Xingyue led the Left Army to attack the Right Army before the palace gate where guards stood.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening Jipeng repeatedly memorialized asking the carriage to depart. Then Xingyue led the Left Army to attack the Right Army before the palace gate where guards stood.

sentences.zh: 繼鵬復縱火焚宮門，煙炎蔽天。

translations.literal: Jipeng again set fire to the palace gates; smoke and flames filled the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Jipeng again set fire to the palace gates; smoke and flames filled the sky.

sentences.zh: 時有鹽州六都兵屯京師，素為兩軍所憚，上急召令入衛；

translations.literal: At the time Salt Prefecture Six-Capital troops were stationed in the capital and both armies had long feared them. The emperor urgently summoned them to enter and guard;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Salt Prefecture Six-Capital troops were stationed in the capital and both armies had long feared them. The emperor urgently summoned them to enter and guard;

sentences.zh: 既至，兩軍退走，各歸邠州及鳳翔。

translations.literal: when they arrived both armies withdrew, each returning to Bin and Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: when they arrived both armies withdrew, each returning to Bin and Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 城中大亂，互相剽掠，上與諸王及親近幸李筠營，護蹕都頭李居實帥眾繼至。

translations.literal: Great chaos reigned in the city with mutual plunder. The emperor, princes, and intimates fled to Li Yun's camp; Protecting the Imperial Procession director Li Jushi led troops and followed.
translations.idiomatic: Great chaos reigned in the city with mutual plunder. The emperor, princes, and intimates fled to Li Yun's camp; Protecting the Imperial Procession director Li Jushi led troops and followed.

sentences.zh: 或傳王行瑜、李茂貞欲自來迎車駕，上懼為所迫，辛酉，以筠、居實兩都兵自衛，出啟夏門，趣南山，宿莎城鎮。

translations.literal: Some reported that Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen wished to come themselves to welcome the carriage. The emperor feared being forced by them. On xinyou he took Yun's and Jushi's two-capital troops as escort, left through Qixia Gate toward the southern mountains, and lodged at Shacheng town.
translations.idiomatic: Some reported that Wang Xingyu and Li Maozhen wished to come themselves to welcome the carriage. The emperor feared being forced by them. On xinyou he took Yun's and Jushi's two-capital troops as escort, left through Qixia Gate toward the southern mountains, and lodged at Shacheng town.

sentences.zh: 士民追從車駕者數十萬人，比至谷口，暍死者三之一，夜，復為盜所掠，哭聲震山谷。

translations.literal: Tens of thousands of common people followed the carriage. By the time they reached the valley mouth one-third had died of heatstroke. At night bandits looted again and wailing shook the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Tens of thousands of common people followed the carriage. By the time they reached the valley mouth one-third had died of heatstroke. At night bandits looted again and wailing shook the mountains.

sentences.zh: 時百官多扈從不及，戶部尚書、判度支及鹽鐵轉運使薛王知柔獨先至，上命權知中書事及置頓使。

translations.literal: Many officials could not keep up with the escort. Minister of Revenue, acting head of the Ministry and salt and iron transport commissioner Prince of Xue Zhirou alone arrived first. The emperor ordered him to act as head of the Secretariat and provision supply commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Many officials could not keep up with the escort. Minister of Revenue, acting head of the Ministry and salt and iron transport commissioner Prince of Xue Zhirou alone arrived first. The emperor ordered him to act as head of the Secretariat and provision supply commissioner.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，李克用入同州。

translations.literal: On renxu Li Keyong entered Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Li Keyong entered Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯、徐彥若、王摶至莎城。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei, Xu Yanruo, and Wang Tuan reached Shacheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei, Xu Yanruo, and Wang Tuan reached Shacheng.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上徙幸石門鎮，命薛王知柔與知樞密院劉光裕還京城，制置守衛宮禁。

translations.literal: On jiazi the emperor moved to Shimen town and ordered Prince of Xue Zhirou and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Liu Guangyu to return to the capital and arrange guard of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor moved to Shimen town and ordered Prince of Xue Zhirou and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Liu Guangyu to return to the capital and arrange guard of the palace.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，李克用遣節度判官王瑰奉表問起居。

translations.literal: On bingyin Li Keyong sent his military adjutant Wang Gui with a memorial inquiring after the emperor's health.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Li Keyong sent his military adjutant Wang Gui with a memorial inquiring after the emperor's health.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上遣內侍郗廷昱繼詔詣李克用軍，令與王珂各發萬騎同赴新平。

translations.literal: On dingmao the emperor sent palace attendant Xi Tingyu with further orders to Keyong's army, directing Keyong and Ke each to send ten thousand horsemen together to Xingping.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the emperor sent palace attendant Xi Tingyu with further orders to Keyong's army, directing Keyong and Ke each to send ten thousand horsemen together to Xingping.

sentences.zh: 又詔彰義節度使張鐇以涇原兵控扼鳳翔。

translations.literal: He also ordered Zhang Yi, military governor of Zhangyi, to use Jingyuan troops to hold and block Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Zhang Yi, military governor of Zhangyi, to use Jingyuan troops to hold and block Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣兵攻華州；

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent troops to attack Hua Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent troops to attack Hua Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 韓建登城呼曰：「僕於李公未嘗失禮，何為見攻？」

translations.literal: Han Jian climbed the wall and shouted, "I have never been discourteous to Lord Li—why am I being attacked?"
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian climbed the wall and shouted, "I have never been discourteous to Lord Li—why am I being attacked?"

sentences.zh: 克用使謂之曰：「公為人臣，逼逐天子，公為有禮，孰為無禮者乎！」

translations.literal: Keyong's messenger replied, "As a subject you drove out the Son of Heaven. If you have courtesy, who lacks it!"
translations.idiomatic: Keyong's messenger replied, "As a subject you drove out the Son of Heaven. If you have courtesy, who lacks it!"

sentences.zh: 會郗廷昱至，言李茂貞將兵三萬至盩厔，王行瑜將兵至興平，皆欲迎車駕，克用乃釋華州之圍，移兵營渭橋。

translations.literal: When Xi Tingyu arrived he reported that Li Maozhen was bringing thirty thousand troops to Zhouzhi and Wang Xingyu's troops had reached Xingping, both wishing to welcome the carriage. Keyong then lifted the siege of Hua and moved his camp to Wei Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Xi Tingyu arrived he reported that Li Maozhen was bringing thirty thousand troops to Zhouzhi and Wang Xingyu's troops had reached Xingping, both wishing to welcome the carriage. Keyong then lifted the siege of Hua and moved his camp to Wei Bridge.

sentences.zh: 以薛王知柔為清海節度使、同平章事，仍權知京兆尹、判度支，充鹽鐵轉運使，俟反正日赴鎮。

translations.literal: Prince of Xue Zhirou was made military governor of Qinghai and Director of the Chancellery, still acting mayor of Jingzhao and head of the Ministry, and salt and iron transport commissioner, to take up his post when order was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xue Zhirou was made military governor of Qinghai and Director of the Chancellery, still acting mayor of Jingzhao and head of the Ministry, and salt and iron transport commissioner, to take up his post when order was restored.

sentences.zh: 上在南山旬餘，士民從車駕避亂者日相驚曰：「邠、岐兵至矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor had been on the southern mountains more than ten days. Common people fleeing with the carriage daily panicked one another, crying, "Bin and Qi troops are coming!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been on the southern mountains more than ten days. Common people fleeing with the carriage daily panicked one another, crying, "Bin and Qi troops are coming!"

sentences.zh: 上遣延王戒丕詣河中，趣李克用令進兵。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Prince of Yan Jiepi to Hezhong to urge Li Keyong to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Prince of Yan Jiepi to Hezhong to urge Li Keyong to advance.

sentences.zh: 壬午，克用發河中。

translations.literal: On renwu Keyong departed Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu Keyong departed Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 八月，上遣供奉官張承業詣克用軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the emperor sent attendant official Zhang Chengye to Keyong's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the emperor sent attendant official Zhang Chengye to Keyong's army.

sentences.zh: 承業，同州人，屢奉使於克用，因留監其軍。

translations.literal: Chengye was a native of Tongzhou who had often been envoy to Keyong and therefore stayed to oversee his army.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye was a native of Tongzhou who had often been envoy to Keyong and therefore stayed to oversee his army.

sentences.zh: 己丑，克用進軍渭橋，遣其將李存貞為前鋒；

translations.literal: On jichou Keyong advanced to Wei Bridge and sent his general Li Cunzhen as vanguard;
translations.idiomatic: On jichou Keyong advanced to Wei Bridge and sent his general Li Cunzhen as vanguard;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，撥永壽，又遣史儼將三千騎詣石門侍衛。

translations.literal: on xinmao he took Yongshou and also sent Shi Yan with three thousand horsemen to Shimen to guard the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: on xinmao he took Yongshou and also sent Shi Yan with three thousand horsemen to Shimen to guard the emperor.

sentences.zh: 癸已，遣李存信、李存審會保大節度使李思孝攻王行瑜黎園寨，擒其將王令陶等，獻於行在。

translations.literal: On guisi he sent Li Cunxin and Li Cunshen to join Baoda military governor Li Sixiao in attacking Wang Xingyu's Liyuan stockade, capturing his generals Wang Lingtao and others and presenting them at the travelling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi he sent Li Cunxin and Li Cunshen to join Baoda military governor Li Sixiao in attacking Wang Xingyu's Liyuan stockade, capturing his generals Wang Lingtao and others and presenting them at the travelling palace.

sentences.zh: 思孝本姓拓跋，思恭之弟也。

translations.literal: Sixiao was originally surnamed Toba and was the younger brother of Sigong.
translations.idiomatic: Sixiao was originally surnamed Toba and was the younger brother of Sigong.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞懼，斬李繼鵬，傳首行在，上表請罪，且遣使求和於克用。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen was afraid. He beheaded Li Jipeng and sent his head to the travelling palace, submitted a memorial begging pardon, and also sent envoys seeking peace with Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen was afraid. He beheaded Li Jipeng and sent his head to the travelling palace, submitted a memorial begging pardon, and also sent envoys seeking peace with Keyong.

sentences.zh: 上復遣延王戒丕、丹王允諭克用，令且赦茂貞，並力討行瑜，俟其殄平，當更與卿議之。

translations.literal: The emperor again sent Prince of Yan Jiepi and Prince of Dan Yun to instruct Keyong to pardon Maozhen for now and join forces against Xingyu; when Xingyu was destroyed they would discuss further with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again sent Prince of Yan Jiepi and Prince of Dan Yun to instruct Keyong to pardon Maozhen for now and join forces against Xingyu; when Xingyu was destroyed they would discuss further with him.

sentences.zh: 且命二王拜克用為兄。

translations.literal: He also ordered the two princes to address Keyong as elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the two princes to address Keyong as elder brother.

sentences.zh: 以前河中節度使崔胤為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Former Hezhong military governor Cui Yin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Former Hezhong military governor Cui Yin was made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，削奪王行瑜官爵。

translations.literal: On wuxu Wang Xingyu's rank and titles were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu Wang Xingyu's rank and titles were stripped.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以李克用為邠寧四面行營都招討使，保大節度使李思孝為北面招討使，定難節度使李思諫為東面招討使，彰義節度使張鐇為西面招討使。

translations.literal: On guimao Li Keyong was made commander-in-chief of all four sides' campaign against Binning; Baoda military governor Li Sixiao was northern campaign commander; Dingnan military governor Li Sijian was eastern campaign commander; Zhangyi military governor Zhang Yi was western campaign commander.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Li Keyong was made commander-in-chief of all four sides' campaign against Binning; Baoda military governor Li Sixiao was northern campaign commander; Dingnan military governor Li Sijian was eastern campaign commander; Zhangyi military governor Zhang Yi was western campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 克用遣其子存勖詣行在，年十一，上奇其狀貌，撫之曰：「兒方為國之棟樑，它日宜盡忠於吾家。」

translations.literal: Keyong sent his son Cunxu to the travelling palace. He was eleven years old. The emperor marvelled at his appearance and stroked him, saying, "Child, you will be the nation's pillar; one day you should be loyal to our house."
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent his son Cunxu to the travelling palace. He was eleven years old. The emperor marvelled at his appearance and stroked him, saying, "Child, you will be the nation's pillar; one day you should be loyal to our house."

sentences.zh: 克用表請上還京；

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized asking the emperor to return to the capital;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong memorialized asking the emperor to return to the capital;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 令克用遣騎三千駐三橋為備御。

translations.literal: He ordered Keyong to post three thousand horsemen at Sanqiao as guard.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Keyong to post three thousand horsemen at Sanqiao as guard.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，車駕還京師。

translations.literal: On xinhai the imperial carriage returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai the imperial carriage returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 壬子，司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事崔昭緯罷為右僕射。

translations.literal: On renzi Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery Cui Zhaowei was dismissed and made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Director of the Chancellery Cui Zhaowei was dismissed and made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以護國留後王珂、盧龍留後劉仁恭各為本鎮節度使。

translations.literal: Huguo military deputy Wang Ke and Lulong military deputy Liu Rengong were each made military governors of their own circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ke, acting governor of Huguo, and Liu Rengong, acting governor of Lulong, were each confirmed as military governors of their respective circuits.

sentences.zh: 時宮室焚毀，未暇完葺，上寓居尚書省，百官往往無袍笏僕馬。

translations.literal: At the time the palace halls had been burned and destroyed, and there was no leisure to complete repairs; the emperor lodged in the Department of State Affairs, and many officials often lacked court robes, tablets, attendants, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The palace had been burned in the fighting, and there was no time yet to rebuild it. The emperor took up residence in the Department of State Affairs, and many officials lacked even court robes, official tablets, servants, and mounts.

sentences.zh: 以李克用為行營都統。

translations.literal: Li Keyong was made supreme commander of the campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong was appointed supreme commander of the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 九月，癸亥，司空兼門下侍郎、同平章事孔緯薨。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on guihai, Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Chancellery Kong Wei died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on guihai, Kong Wei—Minister of Works, Vice Director of the Chancellery, and Director of the Chancellery—passed away.

sentences.zh: 辛未，朱全忠自將擊朱瑄，戰於梁山；

translations.literal: On xinwei Zhu Quanzhong personally led troops to attack Zhu Xuan; they fought at Liangshan;
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei Zhu Quanzhong personally took the field against Zhu Xuan, and the two armies clashed at Liangshan;

sentences.zh: 瑄敗走還鄆。

translations.literal: Xuan was defeated, fled, and returned to Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan was routed and fled back to Yan.

sentences.zh: 李克用急攻梨園，王行瑜求救於李茂貞，茂貞遣兵萬人屯龍泉鎮，自將兵三萬屯咸陽之旁。

translations.literal: Li Keyong pressed the attack on Liyuan. Wang Xingyu sought rescue from Li Maozhen. Maozhen sent ten thousand troops to encamp at Longquan garrison and personally led thirty thousand troops to camp beside Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong pressed his assault on Liyuan. Wang Xingyu appealed to Li Maozhen for help. Maozhen dispatched ten thousand men to hold Longquan garrison and personally led thirty thousand to encamp near Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 克用請詔茂貞歸鎮，仍削奪其官爵，欲分兵討之。

translations.literal: Keyong requested an edict ordering Maozhen to return to his circuit, and furthermore to strip him of rank and titles, intending to detach troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong asked the throne to order Maozhen back to his own territory, strip him of rank and titles, and let Keyong detach forces to punish him.

sentences.zh: 上以茂貞自誅繼鵬，前已赦宥，不可復削奪誅討，但詔歸鎮，仍令克用與之和解。

translations.literal: The emperor held that since Maozhen had himself executed Jipeng and had already been pardoned before, he could not again be stripped and punished by attack; he only ordered Maozhen to return to his circuit and still directed Keyong to make peace with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied that Maozhen had already executed Li Jipeng with his own hand and had been pardoned once; he could not be stripped and attacked again. Maozhen was merely ordered home, and Keyong was told to reconcile with him.

sentences.zh: 以昭義節度使李罕之檢校侍中，充邠寧四面行營副都統。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi military governor Li Hanzhi was appointed honorary palace attendant and served as deputy supreme commander of the Binning four-side campaign headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi, military governor of Zhaoyi, was made honorary palace attendant and deputy supreme commander of the four-sided campaign against Binning.

sentences.zh: 史儼敗邠寧兵於雲陽，擒雲陽鎮使王令誨等，獻之。

translations.literal: Shi Yan defeated Binning troops at Yunyang, captured Yunyang garrison commissioner Wang Linghui and others, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Yan routed Binning forces at Yunyang, captured the Yunyang garrison commissioner Wang Linghui and others, and sent them up as prisoners.

sentences.zh: 王建遣簡州刺史王宗瑤等將兵赴難；

translations.literal: Wang Jian sent Jianzhou prefect Wang Zongyao and others to lead troops to rush to the emperor's aid;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian sent Jianzhou prefect Wang Zongyao and others with an army to march to the emperor's relief;

sentences.zh: 甲戌，軍於綿州。

translations.literal: On jiaxu they encamped at Mianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu the force halted at Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 董昌求救於楊行密，行密遣泗州防禦使台濛攻蘇州以救之，且表昌引咎，願修職貢，請復官爵。

translations.literal: Dong Chang sought rescue from Yang Xingmi. Xingmi sent Sizhou defense commissioner Tai Meng to attack Suzhou to relieve him, and also memorialized that Chang acknowledged guilt, wished to resume tribute duties, and requested restoration of rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang begged Yang Xingmi for help. Xingmi sent Sizhou defense commissioner Tai Meng to strike Suzhou and lift the pressure on him, while also memorializing that Chang accepted blame, wished to resume tribute, and asked that his rank and titles be restored.

sentences.zh: 又遺錢鏐書，稱：「昌狂疾自立，已畏兵諫，執送同惡。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Qian Liu, stating: "Chang's madness in declaring himself [emperor] has already been curbed by armed remonstrance; I have seized and delivered his accomplices.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Qian Liu, saying: "Chang's delusion in proclaiming himself emperor has already been checked by force; I have seized his fellow conspirators and handed them over.

sentences.zh: 不當復伐之。」

translations.literal: He should not be attacked again."
translations.idiomatic: There is no cause to attack him again."

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丙戌，河東將李存貞敗邠寧軍於梨園北，殺千餘人。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on bingxu, Hedong general Li Cunzhen defeated Binning army north of Liyuan, killing more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on bingxu, Hedong general Li Cunzhen routed Binning forces north of Liyuan and killed more than a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 自是梨園閉壁不敢出。

translations.literal: From then on Liyuan shut its walls and dared not sally forth.
translations.idiomatic: After that the garrison at Liyuan closed its gates and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 貶右僕射崔昭緯為梧州司馬。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director Cui Zhaowei was demoted to Administrator of Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Cui Zhaowei was demoted to administrator of Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 魏國夫人陳氏，才色冠後宮；

translations.literal: Lady of Wei State, née Chen, in talent and beauty surpassed all in the inner palace;
translations.idiomatic: Lady Chen, the Lady of Wei State, was the most gifted and beautiful woman in the inner palace;

sentences.zh: 戊子，上以賜李克用。

translations.literal: On wuzi the emperor bestowed her upon Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the emperor gave her to Li Keyong as a gift.

sentences.zh: 克用令李罕之、李存信等急攻梨園；

translations.literal: Keyong ordered Li Hanzhi, Li Cunxin, and others to press the attack on Liyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong ordered Li Hanzhi, Li Cunxin, and others to storm Liyuan without delay;

sentences.zh: 城中食盡，棄城走。

translations.literal: Food in the city was exhausted; they abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions inside the city ran out, the defenders abandoned the place and fled.

sentences.zh: 罕之等邀擊之，所殺萬餘人，克梨園等三寨，獲王行瑜子知進及大將李元福等；

translations.literal: Hanzhi and others intercepted them, killing more than ten thousand; they captured three fortified camps including Liyuan, seizing Wang Xingyu's son Zhijin and great generals Li Yuanfu and others;
translations.idiomatic: Hanzhi and the others cut them off in pursuit, killing more than ten thousand men. They took three camps, including Liyuan, and captured Wang Xingyu's son Zhijin, the great general Li Yuanfu, and others;

sentences.zh: 克用進屯梨園。

translations.literal: Keyong advanced and encamped at Liyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong moved forward and made camp at Liyuan.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，王行約、王行實燒寧州遁去。

translations.literal: On gengyin Wang Xingyue and Wang Xingshi burned Ningzhou and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Wang Xingyue and Wang Xingshi torched Ningzhou and slipped away.

sentences.zh: 克用奏請以匡國節度使蘇文建為靜難節度使，趣令赴鎮，且理寧州，招撫降人。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized requesting that Kuangguo military governor Su Wenjian be made Jingnan military governor, urged to proceed to his post, and also to administer Ningzhou and receive and pacify those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong memorialized asking that Su Wenjian, military governor of Kuangguo, be appointed military governor of Jingnan, sent at once to take up his post, put Ningzhou in order, and receive and pacify the surrendered population.

sentences.zh: 上遷居大內。

translations.literal: The emperor moved his residence into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor moved back into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣都將葛從周擊兗州，自以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent commander Ge Congzhou to attack Yanzhou, himself following with the main army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent his commander Ge Congzhou against Yanzhou and followed with the main army himself.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，圍兗州。

translations.literal: On guimao they besieged Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao they laid siege to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣寧國節度使田頵、潤州團練使安仁義攻杭州鎮戍以救董昌，昌使湖州將徐淑會淮南將魏約共圍嘉興。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent Ningguo military governor Tian Yun and Runzhou training commissioner An Renyi to attack Hangzhou garrison posts to rescue Dong Chang; Chang sent Huzhou general Xu Shu to join with Huainan general Wei Yue in jointly besieging Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Ningguo military governor Tian Yun and Runzhou training commissioner An Renyi to strike Hangzhou's outlying garrisons and relieve Dong Chang. Chang, for his part, sent the Huzhou general Xu Shu to join Huainan general Wei Yue in a joint siege of Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐遣武勇都指揮使顧全武救嘉興，破烏墩、光福二寨。

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent martial commander Gu Quanwu to rescue Jiaxing, breaking Wudun and Guangfu camps.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent his martial commander Gu Quanwu to relieve Jiaxing and overran the camps at Wudun and Guangfu.

sentences.zh: 淮南將柯厚破蘇州水柵。

translations.literal: Huainan general Ke Hou broke Suzhou's river barriers.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan general Ke Hou smashed Suzhou's river palisades.

sentences.zh: 全武，餘姚人也。

translations.literal: Quanwu was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Quanwu was a man of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 義武節度使王處存薨，軍中推其子節度副使郜為留後。

translations.literal: Yiwu military governor Wang Chucun died; the army pushed his son, deputy military governor Gao, as military deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chucun, military governor of Yiwu, died, and the army chose his son Gao, the deputy military governor, as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 以京兆尹武邑孫偓為兵部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: Metropolitan Prefect of Jingzhao, from Wuyi, Sun Wo was made Vice Minister of War and Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Wo of Wuyi, metropolitan prefect of Jingzhao, was appointed Vice Minister of War and Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 王行瑜以精甲五千守龍泉寨，李克用攻之。

translations.literal: Wang Xingyu with five thousand crack troops defended Longquan camp; Li Keyong attacked it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu held Longquan camp with five thousand elite troops while Li Keyong assaulted it.

sentences.zh: 李茂貞以兵五千救之，營於鎮西。

translations.literal: Li Maozhen with five thousand troops came to rescue him, encamping at Zhenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Maozhen brought five thousand men to his relief and encamped west of the garrison town.

sentences.zh: 李罕之擊鳳翔兵，走之，十一月，丁巳，撥龍泉寨。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi struck Fengxiang troops and routed them; in the eleventh month, on dingsi, Longquan camp was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi attacked the Fengxiang force and drove it off. In the eleventh month, on dingsi, Longquan camp fell.

sentences.zh: 行瑜走入邠州，遣使請降於克用。

translations.literal: Xingyu fled into Binzhou and sent envoys seeking surrender from Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Xingyu fled into Bin Prefecture and sent envoys offering to surrender to Keyong.

sentences.zh: 齊州刺史朱瓊舉州降於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Qizhou prefect Zhu Qiong surrendered the prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qiong, prefect of Qizhou, surrendered the entire prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 瓊，瑾之從父兄也。

translations.literal: Qiong was a paternal cousin of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was Zhu Jin's elder cousin on his father's side.

sentences.zh: 衢州刺史陳儒卒，弟岌代之。

translations.literal: Quzhou prefect Chen Ru died; his younger brother Ji replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Ru, prefect of Quzhou, died, and his younger brother Ji succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 李克用引兵逼邠州，王行瑜登城，號哭謂克用曰：「行瑜無罪，迫脅乘輿，皆李茂貞及李繼鵬所為。

translations.literal: Li Keyong led troops to press Binzhou. Wang Xingyu ascended the wall, wailing and saying to Keyong: "Xingyu is guiltless; coercing the imperial carriage was all done by Li Maozhen and Li Jipeng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong marched his army up to Bin Prefecture. Wang Xingyu climbed the wall, weeping, and cried out to Keyong: "I am innocent! The coercion of the emperor's carriage was the work of Li Maozhen and Li Jipeng alone.

sentences.zh: 請移兵問鳳翔，行瑜願束身歸朝。」
