translations.literal: I ask you to shift troops to question Fengxiang; Xingyu is willing to submit himself and return to court."
translations.idiomatic: Turn your army against Fengxiang, and I will submit myself and return to court."

sentences.zh: 克用曰：「王尚父何恭之甚！

translations.literal: Keyong said: "Wang Shangfu, how excessively deferential you are!
translations.idiomatic: Keyong replied: "Wang Shangfu, you grovel too much!

sentences.zh: 僕受詔討三賊臣，公預其一，束身歸朝，非僕所得專也。」

translations.literal: I received an edict to punish three treacherous ministers; you are one of them. Submitting yourself to court is not within my sole authority."
translations.idiomatic: I was ordered to punish three rebel ministers, and you are one of them. Whether you may submit yourself to the throne is not for me alone to decide."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，行瑜挈族棄城走。

translations.literal: On dingmao Xingyu took his clan, abandoned the city, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Xingyu fled the city with his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 克用入邠州，封府庫，撫居人，命指揮使高爽權巡撫軍城，奏趣蘇文建赴鎮。

translations.literal: Keyong entered Binzhou, sealed the treasury, comforted the inhabitants, ordered commander Gao Shuang to provisionally patrol the garrison city, and memorialized urging Su Wenjian to proceed to his post.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong entered Bin Prefecture, sealed the treasury, reassured the populace, and put commander Gao Shuang in charge of the garrison city on a provisional basis. He also memorialized urging Su Wenjian to take up his post at once.

sentences.zh: 行瑜走至慶州境，部下斬行瑜，傳首。

translations.literal: Xingyu fled to the borders of Qingzhou; his subordinates beheaded Xingyu and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: As Xingyu fled into Qing Prefecture, his own followers cut off his head and sent it in.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄遣其將賀瑰、柳存及河東將何懷寶將兵萬餘人襲曹州，以解兗州之圍。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan sent his generals He Gui, Liu Cun, and Hedong general He Huaibao with more than ten thousand troops to raid Caozhou, to relieve the siege of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan sent his generals He Gui and Liu Cun, together with Hedong general He Huaibao and more than ten thousand men, to strike Caozhou and break the siege of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 瑰，濮陽人也。

translations.literal: Gui was a native of Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui was a man of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，全忠自中都引兵夜追之，比明，至巨野南，及之，屠殺殆盡，生擒瑰存、懷寶，俘士卒三千餘人，是日晡後，大風沙塵晦冥，全忠曰：「此殺人未足耳！」

translations.literal: On dingmao Quanzhong from Zhongdu led troops in night pursuit; by dawn he reached south of Juye, caught up with them, and slaughtered nearly all; he captured Gui, Cun, and Huaibao alive and took more than three thousand soldiers prisoner. That day after the hour of shen, a great wind raised dust and sand until the sky was dark. Quanzhong said: "This killing is still not enough!"
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Quanzhong marched out of Zhongdu by night in pursuit. At daybreak he reached the south of Juye, overtook the enemy, and butchered nearly the entire force. He took He Gui, Liu Cun, and He Huaibao alive and captured more than three thousand soldiers. That afternoon a gale blew dust until the sky turned black. Quanzhong said, "This is still not enough blood!"

sentences.zh: 下令所得之俘盡殺之。

translations.literal: He ordered all prisoners taken to be killed.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered every captive put to the sword.

sentences.zh: 庚午，縛瑰等徇於兗州城下，謂朱瑾曰：「卿兄已敗，何不早降！」

translations.literal: On gengwu he bound Gui and the others and paraded them beneath the walls of Yanzhou, saying to Zhu Jin: "Your elder brother has already been defeated—why not surrender early!"
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu he had Gui and the others bound and displayed beneath the walls of Yanzhou, shouting up to Zhu Jin: "Your brother is already beaten—why not surrender while you still can!"

sentences.zh: 丁丑，雅州刺史王宗侃攻撥利州，執刺史李繼顒，斬之。

translations.literal: On dingchou Yazhou prefect Wang Zongkan attacked and took Lizhou, seized prefect Li Jiyong, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou Wang Zongkan, prefect of Yazhou, stormed Lizhou, seized its prefect Li Jiyong, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 朱瑾偽遣使請降於朱全忠，全忠自就延壽門下與瑾語。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin falsely sent envoys requesting surrender to Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong himself went beneath the Yanshou Gate to speak with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin sent envoys under false pretenses offering to surrender to Zhu Quanzhong. Quanzhong went in person to the Yanshou Gate to speak with him.

sentences.zh: 瑾曰：「欲送符印，願使兄瓊來領之。」

translations.literal: Jin said: "I wish to deliver the seal and tally; I ask that you send my elder brother Qiong to receive them."
translations.idiomatic: Jin said, "I am ready to hand over the seal and tally, but I ask that my elder brother Qiong be sent to receive them."

sentences.zh: 辛巳，全忠使瓊往，瑾立馬橋上，伏驍果董懷進於橋下，瓊至，懷進突出，擒之以入，須臾，擲首城外。

translations.literal: On xinsi Quanzhong sent Qiong. Jin stood on Ma Bridge with crack trooper Dong Huaijin hidden beneath the bridge. When Qiong arrived Huaijin burst forth, seized him and dragged him inside; in a moment his head was thrown outside the walls.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi Quanzhong sent Qiong forward. Jin waited on Horse Bridge while his crack trooper Dong Huaijin lay hidden beneath it. When Qiong arrived, Huaijin sprang out, seized him, and dragged him inside; a moment later Qiong's head was thrown over the wall.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃引兵還，以瓊弟玭為齊州防禦使，殺柳存、何懷寶；

translations.literal: Quanzhong then withdrew his troops, made Qiong's younger brother Min Qizhou defense commissioner, and executed Liu Cun and He Huaibao;
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then withdrew his army, appointed Qiong's younger brother Min defense commissioner of Qizhou, and executed Liu Cun and He Huaibao;

sentences.zh: 聞賀瑰名，釋而用之。

translations.literal: Hearing He Gui's reputation, he released and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard He Gui's reputation, he spared him and put him in service.

sentences.zh: 李克用旋軍渭北。

translations.literal: Li Keyong rotated his army to the north of the Wei River.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong withdrew his army to the north bank of the Wei River.

sentences.zh: 加靜難節度使蘇文建同平章事。

translations.literal: Jingnan military governor Su Wenjian was additionally made Director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wenjian, military governor of Jingnan, was additionally appointed Director of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 蔣勳求為邵州刺史，劉建鋒不許，勳乃與鄧繼崇起兵，連飛山、梅山蠻寇湘潭，據邵州，使其將申德昌屯定勝鎮以扼潭人。

translations.literal: Jiang Xun sought to be Shaozhou prefect; Liu Jianfeng refused. Xun then raised troops with Deng Jichong, linking Feishan and Meishan barbarians to raid Xiangtan, seized Shaozhou, and sent his general Shen Dechang to encamp at Dingsheng garrison to block men from Tan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Xun sought appointment as prefect of Shaozhou, but Liu Jianfeng refused him. Xun then rose in arms with Deng Jichong, rallied the Feishan and Meishan tribes to raid Xiangtan, seized Shaozhou, and posted his general Shen Dechang at Dingsheng garrison to choke off access from Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲申，閬州防禦使李繼雍、蓬州刺史費存、渠州刺史陳璠各帥所部兵奔王建。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiashen, Langzhou defense commissioner Li Jiyong, Pengzhou prefect Fei Cun, and Qu Prefecture prefect Chen Fan each led their troops to flee to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiashen, Li Jiyong, defense commissioner of Langzhou; Fei Cun, prefect of Pengzhou; and Chen Fan, prefect of Qu Prefecture, each led their forces in flight to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，李克用軍於雲陽。

translations.literal: On yiyou Li Keyong encamped at Yunyang.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou Li Keyong encamped at Yunyang.

sentences.zh: 王建奏：「東川節度使顧彥暉不發兵赴難，而掠奪輜重，遣瀘州刺史馬敬儒斷峽路，請興兵討之。」

translations.literal: Wang Jian memorialized: "Dongchuan military governor Gu Yanhui did not send troops to the emperor's aid but plundered baggage trains and sent Luzhou prefect Ma Jingru to cut the gorge routes; I request permission to raise troops to punish him."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian memorialized: "Gu Yanhui, military governor of Dongchuan, failed to march to the emperor's relief and instead looted the baggage train. He sent Luzhou prefect Ma Jingru to block the gorge routes. I ask permission to raise troops and punish him."

sentences.zh: 戊子，華洪大破東川兵於楸林，俘斬數萬，拔揪林寒。

translations.literal: On wuzi Hua Hong greatly defeated Dongchuan troops at Qiulin, capturing and killing tens of thousands, and took Qiulin and Hangu.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi Hua Hong routed the Dongchuan army at Qiulin, capturing and killing tens of thousands of men and seizing Qiulin and Hangu.

sentences.zh: 乙未，進李克用爵晉王，加李罕之兼侍中，以河東大將蓋寓領容管觀察使；

translations.literal: On yiwei Li Keyong was advanced in rank to Prince of Jin; Li Hanzhi was additionally made Palace Attendant; Hedong great general Gai Yu was made Rongguan observation commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Li Keyong was elevated to Prince of Jin; Li Hanzhi was additionally made Palace Attendant; and the great Hedong general Gai Yu was made observation commissioner of Rongguan;

sentences.zh: 自餘克用將佐、子孫並進官爵。

translations.literal: Keyong's other commanders, aides, and descendants were all advanced in rank and titles.
translations.idiomatic: All of Keyong's other commanders, aides, and descendants were likewise promoted in rank and title.

sentences.zh: 克用性嚴急，左右小有過輒死，無敢違忤；

translations.literal: Keyong's nature was stern and harsh; those around him died for the slightest fault, and none dared disobey;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was severe and quick-tempered; attendants who erred even slightly were put to death, and no one dared defy him;

sentences.zh: 惟蓋寓敏慧，能揣其意，婉辭裨益，無不從者。

translations.literal: Only Gai Yu was quick-witted, able to read his intent; with tactful words he offered benefit, and there was nothing to which Keyong did not assent.
translations.idiomatic: Only Gai Yu was clever enough to read his mind. With tactful counsel he could steer Keyong, and Keyong never refused him.

sentences.zh: 克用或以非罪怒將吏，寓必陽助之怒，克用常釋之；

translations.literal: When Keyong in wrongful anger raged at commanders and officials, Yu would always outwardly join in the anger, and Keyong would usually release them;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Keyong flew into unjust rage at a commander or official, Yu would pretend to share his fury—and Keyong would usually let the man go;

sentences.zh: 有所諫諍，必征近事為喻；

translations.literal: when he offered remonstrance he always cited recent events as analogies;
translations.idiomatic: when he remonstrated, he always illustrated his point with recent events;

sentences.zh: 由是克用愛信之，境內無不依附，權與克用侔。

translations.literal: therefore Keyong loved and trusted him; within the territory none failed to attach themselves to him, and his power matched Keyong's.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong therefore loved and trusted him. Everyone in the territory looked to him, and his authority rivaled Keyong's own.

sentences.zh: 朝廷及鄰道遣使至河東，其賞賜賂遺，先入克用，次及寓家。

translations.literal: When the court and neighboring circuits sent envoys to Hedong, their rewards and gifts first reached Keyong, then Gai Yu's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the court or neighboring circuits sent envoys to Hedong, rewards and gifts went first to Keyong and next to Gai Yu's household.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠數遣數人間之，及揚言雲蓋寓已代克用，而克用待之益厚。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong repeatedly sent men to sow discord between them and spread word that Gai Yu had already replaced Keyong, yet Keyong treated him all the more generously.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong repeatedly sent agents to drive a wedge between them and spread rumors that Gai Yu had already supplanted Keyong—but Keyong treated Yu only more generously.

sentences.zh: 丙申，王建攻東川，別將王宗弼為東川兵所擒，顧彥暉畜以為子，戊戌，通州刺史李彥昭將所部兵二千降於建。

translations.literal: On bingshen Wang Jian attacked Dongchuan; detached commander Wang Zongbi was captured by Dongchuan troops; Gu Yanhui raised him as a son. On wuxu Tongzhou prefect Li Yanzhao led two thousand of his troops to surrender to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen Wang Jian attacked Dongchuan. His detached commander Wang Zongbi was captured by Dongchuan forces, and Gu Yanhui adopted him as a son. On wuxu Li Yanzhao, prefect of Tongzhou, surrendered to Wang Jian with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣掌書記李襲吉入謝恩，密言於上曰：「比年以來，關輔不寧，乘此勝勢，遂取鳳翔，一勞永逸，時不可失。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent chief secretary Li Xiji to enter and give thanks for imperial favor, secretly saying to the emperor: "In recent years the Guanzhong region has not been at peace. Seizing this victorious momentum to take Fengxiang at one effort would bring lasting ease; the moment must not be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent his chief secretary Li Xiji to court to offer thanks, and privately told the emperor: "These past years the capital region has known no peace. Seize this victory and take Fengxiang in one stroke—the trouble will be settled for good. The moment will not come again.

sentences.zh: 臣屯軍渭北，專俟進止。」

translations.literal: Your subject encamps his army north of the Wei River, awaiting only your command to advance or halt."
translations.idiomatic: My army is camped north of the Wei, awaiting your orders alone."

sentences.zh: 上謀於貴近，或曰：「茂貞覆滅，則沙陀大盛，朝廷危矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor consulted close attendants; some said: "If Maozhen is overthrown, then the Shatuo will grow greatly powerful, and the court will be in peril!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted his inner circle. Some said, "If Maozhen is destroyed, the Shatuo will grow too strong and the throne itself will be imperiled!"

sentences.zh: 上乃賜克用詔，褒其忠款，而言：「不臣之狀，行瑜為甚。

translations.literal: The emperor then bestowed an edict on Keyong, praising his loyalty, and stating: "In the matter of disloyalty, Xingyu was the worst.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor therefore sent Keyong an edict praising his loyalty, but adding: "Of all the rebels, Xingyu was the worst.

sentences.zh: 自朕出幸以來，茂貞、韓建自知其罪，不忘國恩，職貢相繼，且當休兵息民。」

translations.literal: Since I went out on tour, Maozhen and Han Jian have known their guilt and not forgotten the state's grace; tribute duties have followed in succession, and it is time to rest the armies and give the people peace."
translations.idiomatic: Since my exile Maozhen and Han Jian have acknowledged their guilt and not forgotten the throne's grace. Their tribute has continued without break. It is time to halt the armies and let the people breathe."

sentences.zh: 克用奉詔而止。

translations.literal: Keyong received the edict and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong obeyed the edict and halted.

sentences.zh: 既而私於詔使曰：「觀朝廷之意，似疑克用有異心也。

translations.literal: Afterward he said privately to the edict envoy: "Judging from the court's intent, it seems to suspect that Keyong harbors a different heart.
translations.idiomatic: Later he told the edict envoy in private, "From the court's tone, it seems the throne suspects me of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 然不去茂貞，關中無安寧之日。」

translations.literal: Yet if Maozhen is not removed, there will be no day of peace in Guanzhong."
translations.idiomatic: But so long as Maozhen remains, Guanzhong will never know peace."

sentences.zh: 又詔免克用入朝，將佐或言：「今密邇闕庭，豈可不入見天子，！」

translations.literal: An edict also exempted Keyong from entering court. Some commanders and aides said: "Now we are close to the imperial precinct—how can we not enter to see the Son of Heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Another edict excused Keyong from coming to court. Some of his commanders urged him: "We are right beside the capital—how can you fail to appear before the Son of Heaven!"

sentences.zh: 克用猶豫未決，蓋寓言於克用曰：「向者王行瑜輩縱兵狂悖，致鑾輿播越，百姓奔散。

translations.literal: Keyong hesitated, undecided. Gai Yu spoke tactfully to Keyong, saying: "Formerly Wang Xingyu and his kind let troops run wild in insolence, causing the imperial carriage to be driven abroad and the people to flee and scatter.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong wavered. Gai Yu said to him carefully: "When Wang Xingyu and his ilk ran riot, they drove the emperor from the capital and sent the people fleeing in every direction.

sentences.zh: 今天子還未安席，人心尚危，大王若引兵渡渭，竊恐復驚駭都邑。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven has only just returned and is not yet settled; hearts are still fearful. If Your Highness leads troops across the Wei, I privately fear the capital will again be shaken in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has only just returned and is not yet secure; the people's hearts are still uneasy. If you cross the Wei with your army, I fear the capital will be thrown into panic again.

sentences.zh: 人臣盡忠，在於勤王，不在入覲，願熟圖之！」

translations.literal: A minister's full loyalty lies in rushing to the emperor's aid, not in entering court for audience; I beg you to consider this carefully!"
translations.idiomatic: A loyal subject proves himself by saving the throne, not by presenting himself at court. Think this through carefully!"

sentences.zh: 克用笑曰：「蓋寓尚不欲吾入朝，況天下之人乎！」

translations.literal: Keyong laughed and said: "Even Gai Yu does not want me to enter court—how much more the people under heaven!"
translations.idiomatic: Keyong laughed and said, "If even Gai Yu does not want me at court, what hope is there with the rest of the empire!"

sentences.zh: 乃表稱：「臣總帥大軍，不敢徑入朝覲，且懼部落士卒侵擾渭北居人。」

translations.literal: He then memorialized, stating: "Your subject commands a great army and dares not enter directly for court audience, and moreover fears that tribal soldiers may harass the inhabitants north of the Wei."
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized: "I command a large army and dare not enter the capital for audience. I also fear my tribal troops may harass the people north of the Wei."

sentences.zh: 辛亥，引兵東歸。

translations.literal: On xinhai he led his troops east and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai he marched east and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 表至京師，上下始安。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached the capital, those above and below at last felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the capital, court and city alike breathed easier.

sentences.zh: 詔賜河東士卒錢三十萬緡。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed three hundred thousand strings of cash on Hedong soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: An edict awarded three hundred thousand strings of cash to the Hedong troops.

sentences.zh: 克用既去，李茂貞驕橫如故，河西州縣多為茂貞所據，以其將胡敬璋為河西節度使。

translations.literal: After Keyong had gone, Li Maozhen was arrogant and overbearing as before; many prefectures and counties west of the river were held by Maozhen, and he made his general Hu Jingzhang military governor of Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: Once Keyong had departed, Li Maozhen was as arrogant as ever. Most of the prefectures and counties west of the river fell under his control, and he appointed his general Hu Jingzhang military governor of Hexi.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠之去兗州也，留葛從周將兵守之，朱瑾閉城不復出，從周將還，乃揚言「天平、河東救兵至，引兵西北邀之，」夜半，潛歸故寨。

translations.literal: When Zhu Quanzhong left Yanzhou he left Ge Congzhou with troops to hold it. Zhu Jin closed the city and did not sally forth again. When Congzhou was about to return, he spread word that "Tianping and Hedong relief troops have arrived," and led troops northwest to intercept them; at midnight he secretly returned to his former camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Quanzhong withdrew from Yanzhou he left Ge Congzhou to hold the city. Zhu Jin shut the gates and refused to come out again. As Congzhou prepared to withdraw, he spread word that "Tianping and Hedong relief forces were approaching," marched northwest as if to intercept them—and at midnight slipped back to his original camp.

sentences.zh: 瑾以從周精兵悉出，果出兵攻寨。

translations.literal: Jin, believing Congzhou's crack troops had all gone out, indeed sent troops to attack the camp.
translations.idiomatic: Believing Congzhou had committed his best troops, Jin duly sallied forth and attacked the camp.

sentences.zh: 從周突出奮擊，殺千餘人，擒其都將孫漢筠而還。

translations.literal: Congzhou sallied forth and fought fiercely, killing over a thousand men, capturing chief officer Sun Hanjun, and returning.
translations.idiomatic: Congzhou burst out in a fierce assault, killed more than a thousand men, captured chief officer Sun Hanjun, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 加鎮海節度使錢鏐兼侍中。

translations.literal: Qian Liu, military governor of Zhenhai, was additionally appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, military governor of Zhenhai, was also made Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 彰義節度使張鐇薨，以其子璉權知留後。

translations.literal: Zhang Ge, military governor of Zhangyi, died; his son Lian was made acting military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ge, military governor of Zhangyi, died, and his son Lian was appointed acting military governor.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄、朱瑾屢為朱全忠所攻，民失耕稼，財力俱弊。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin were repeatedly attacked by Zhu Quanzhong; the people lost their crops, and wealth and strength were both exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan and Zhu Jin suffered repeated attacks from Zhu Quanzhong; the people could no longer farm, and both their wealth and fighting strength were spent.

sentences.zh: 告急於河東，李克用遣大將史儼、李承嗣將數千騎假道於魏以救之。

translations.literal: They urgently requested aid from Hedong; Li Keyong sent great generals Shi Yan and Li Chengsi with several thousand cavalry, requesting passage through Wei to rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: They sent urgent appeals to Hedong, and Li Keyong dispatched his great generals Shi Yan and Li Chengsi with several thousand horsemen by way of Wei to relieve them.

sentences.zh: 安州防禦使家晟與朱全忠親吏蔣玄暉有隙，恐及禍，與指揮使劉士政、兵馬監押陳可璠將兵三千襲桂州，殺經略使周元靜而代之。

translations.literal: Jia Sheng, defense commissioner of Anzhou, had a rift with Zhu Quanzhong's personal clerk Jiang Xuanhui; fearing calamity, together with commander Liu Shizheng and military supervisor Chen Kefan he led three thousand troops in a surprise attack on Guizhou, killed military commissioner Zhou Yuanjing, and replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Sheng, defense commissioner of Anzhou, was at odds with Jiang Xuanhui, a personal clerk of Zhu Quanzhong. Fearing retribution, he joined commander Liu Shizheng and military supervisor Chen Kefan in leading three thousand troops against Guizhou, killed the military commissioner Zhou Yuanjing, and took his place.

sentences.zh: 晟醉侮可璠，可璠手刃之，推士政知軍府事，可璠自為副使。

translations.literal: Sheng, drunk, insulted Kefan; Kefan killed him with his own hand, set up Shizheng to administer the headquarters, and made himself deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, drunk, humiliated Kefan, who killed him on the spot. Kefan then installed Shizheng to run the headquarters and appointed himself deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 詔即以士政為桂管經略使。

translations.literal: An edict immediately appointed Shizheng military commissioner of Guiguan.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict promptly made Shizheng military commissioner of Guiguan.

sentences.zh: 玄暉，吳人也。

translations.literal: Xuanhui was a man of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanhui was a native of Wu.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之下乾寧三年（

translations.literal: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial, Qianning year 3 (
translations.idiomatic: The latter portion of the reign of Emperor Zhaozong, the Sagely, Solemn, Illustrious, Cultured, and Filial — Qianning, year 3 (

sentences.zh: 丙辰，公元八九六年）

translations.literal: bingchen, corresponding to 896 CE).
translations.idiomatic: bingchen, corresponding to 896 CE).

sentences.zh: 春，正月，西川將王宗夔攻拔龍州，殺刺史田昉。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Wang Zongkui, a general of Xichuan, captured Longzhou and killed prefect Tian Fang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, the Xichuan general Wang Zongkui took Longzhou and killed its prefect, Tian Fang.

sentences.zh: 丁已，劉建鋒遣都指揮使馬殷將兵討蔣勳，攻定勝寨，破之。

translations.literal: On disi, Liu Jianfeng sent chief commander Ma Yin with troops to attack Jiang Xun, assaulted Dingsheng Fort, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: On disi, Liu Jianfeng sent his chief commander Ma Yin against Jiang Xun, stormed Dingsheng Fort, and carried it.

sentences.zh: 辛未，安仁義以舟師至湖州，欲渡江應董昌，錢鏐遣武勇都指揮使顧全武、都知兵馬使許再思守西陵，仁義不能度。

translations.literal: On xinwei, An Renyi brought naval forces to Huzhou, intending to cross the river to assist Dong Chang; Qian Liu sent Wu Yong chief commander Gu Quanwu and army inspector Xu Zaisi to hold Xiling, and Renyi could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, An Renyi arrived at Huzhou with a fleet, planning to cross the river to aid Dong Chang. Qian Liu sent Gu Quanwu, chief commander of the Wu Yong corps, and Xu Zaisi, director of military affairs, to defend Xiling, and Renyi was unable to get across.

sentences.zh: 昌遣其將湯臼守石城，袁邠守餘姚。

translations.literal: Chang sent his general Tang Jiu to hold Shicheng and Yuan Bin to hold Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Chang posted his generals Tang Jiu at Shicheng and Yuan Bin at Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 閏月，克用遣蕃、漢都指揮使李存信將萬騎假道於魏以救兗、鄆，軍於莘縣。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Keyong sent the Tangut and Han chief commander Li Cunxin with ten thousand cavalry, requesting passage through Wei to rescue Yan and Yun, and encamped at Shen County.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Li Keyong sent Li Cunxin, chief commander of the Tangut and Han forces, with ten thousand horsemen through Wei to relieve Yan and Yun, and camped at Shen County.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠使人謂羅弘信曰：「克用志吞河朔，師還之日，貴道可憂。」

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent someone to tell Luo Hongxin: "Keyong intends to swallow the region north of the Yellow River; when his army returns, your circuit will be in peril."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent a messenger to Luo Hongxin, saying, "Li Keyong aims to swallow the whole region north of the Yellow River. When his troops march home, your circuit will be in danger."

sentences.zh: 存信戢眾不嚴，侵暴魏人。

translations.literal: Cunxin did not strictly restrain his troops; they plundered the people of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin failed to keep his men in order, and they ravaged the people of Wei.

sentences.zh: 弘信怒，發兵三萬夜襲之。

translations.literal: Hongxin was enraged and sent thirty thousand troops to attack them by night.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Hongxin sent thirty thousand men to strike them in a night attack.

sentences.zh: 存信軍潰退。

translations.literal: Cunxin's army broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxin's army collapsed and retreated.

sentences.zh: 保洺州，喪士卒什二三，委棄資糧兵械萬樓；

translations.literal: He held Mingzhou, lost two or three tenths of his soldiers, and abandoned supplies and weapons in vast quantities;
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to Mingzhou, losing two or three soldiers in ten, and left behind mountains of provisions and arms;

sentences.zh: 史儼、李承嗣之軍隔絕不得還。

translations.literal: the armies of Shi Yan and Li Chengsi were cut off and could not return.
translations.idiomatic: the forces of Shi Yan and Li Chengsi were isolated and unable to get back.

sentences.zh: 弘信自是與河東絕，專志於汴。

translations.literal: From this Hongxin broke with Hedong and devoted himself exclusively to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: After this Hongxin severed ties with Hedong and threw in his lot entirely with Bian.

sentences.zh: 金忠方圖兗、鄆，畏弘信議其後，弘信每有贈遺，全忠必對使者北向拜授之，曰：「六兄於予，倍年以長，固非諸鄰之比。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong was then scheming against Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might attack from the rear; whenever Hongxin sent gifts, Quanzhong always faced north and bowed to receive them from the envoy, saying: "Sixth Elder Brother to me is more than twice my senior in years—he is certainly not to be compared with other neighbors."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong was then pressing Yan and Yun and feared Hongxin might move against his rear. Whenever Hongxin sent presents, Quanzhong would turn north, bow to the messenger, and accept them, saying, "Sixth Elder Brother is more than twice my senior in years—he is no ordinary neighbor."

sentences.zh: 弘信信之，全忠以是得專意東方。

translations.literal: Hongxin believed him, and Quanzhong thereby gained leave to focus exclusively on the east.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxin took him at his word, and Quanzhong was thus free to concentrate wholly on the east.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，果州刺史張雄降於王建。

translations.literal: On dinghai, Zhang Xiong, prefect of Guozhou, surrendered to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Zhang Xiong, prefect of Guozhou, submitted to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 二月，戊辰，顧全武、許再思敗湯臼於石城。

translations.literal: In the second month, on wuchen, Gu Quanwu and Xu Zaisi defeated Tang Jiu at Shicheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on wuchen, Gu Quanwu and Xu Zaisi routed Tang Jiu at Shicheng.

sentences.zh: 上用楊行密之請，赦董昌，復其官爵；

translations.literal: The emperor, at Yang Xingmi's request, pardoned Dong Chang and restored his titles and offices;
translations.idiomatic: At Yang Xingmi's request, the emperor pardoned Dong Chang and restored his rank and titles;

sentences.zh: 錢鏐不從。

translations.literal: Qian Liu refused to comply.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu would not go along.

sentences.zh: 以通王滋判侍衛諸將事。

translations.literal: Tong Wangzi was appointed to oversee the affairs of the imperial guard generals.
translations.idiomatic: Tong Wangzi was put in charge of the palace guard generals.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠薦兵部尚書張濬，上欲復相之；

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong recommended Zhang Jun, Minister of War; the emperor wished to restore him as chief minister;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong recommended Zhang Jun, Minister of War, and the emperor wanted to bring him back as chief minister;

sentences.zh: 李克用表請發兵擊全忠，且言「濬朝為相，臣則夕至闕庭！」

translations.literal: Li Keyong memorialized requesting troops to attack Quanzhong, and said: "If Jun becomes chief minister in the morning, I shall reach the palace gate by evening!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong submitted a memorial asking to march against Quanzhong and declared, "If Zhang Jun becomes chief minister in the morning, I shall be at the palace gates by evening!"

sentences.zh: 京師震懼，上下詔和解之。

translations.literal: The capital was shaken with fear; edicts were issued above and below to reconcile them.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was terrified, and edicts from court and throne alike were issued to patch up the quarrel.

sentences.zh: 三月，以天雄留後李繼徽為節度使。

translations.literal: In the third month, Li Jihui, acting governor of Tianxiong, was appointed military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Li Jihui, acting governor of Tianxiong, was confirmed as military governor.

sentences.zh: 保大節度使李思孝表請致仁，薦弟思敬自代，詔以思孝為太師，致仕，思敬為保大留後。

translations.literal: Li Sixiao, military governor of Baoda, memorialized requesting retirement, recommending his younger brother Sijing to replace him; an edict made Sixiao Grand Preceptor and retired him, and Sijing became acting governor of Baoda.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sixiao, military governor of Baoda, asked to retire and recommended his younger brother Sijing as his successor. An edict made Sixiao Grand Preceptor and released him from office, and Sijing became acting governor of Baoda.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣龐師古將兵伐鄆州，敗鄆兵於馬頰，遂抵其城下。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu with troops to attack Yun Prefecture, defeated Yun troops at Maying, and advanced to the foot of the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu against Yun Prefecture, defeated its army at Maying, and pushed on to the city walls.

sentences.zh: 己酉，顧全武等攻餘姚，明州刺史黃晟遣兵助之；

translations.literal: On jiyou, Gu Quanwu and others attacked Yuyao; Huang Sheng, prefect of Mingzhou, sent troops to assist;
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou, Gu Quanwu and his colleagues assaulted Yuyao, and Huang Sheng, prefect of Mingzhou, sent troops to help;

sentences.zh: 董昌遣其將徐章救餘姚，全武擊擒之。

translations.literal: Dong Chang sent his general Xu Zhang to relieve Yuyao; Quanwu attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang dispatched Xu Zhang to rescue Yuyao, but Quanwu struck and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，辛酉，河漲，將毀滑州城，朱全忠命決為二河，夾滑城而東，為害滋甚。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on xinyou, the Yellow River rose and was about to destroy the walls of Hua Prefecture; Zhu Quanzhong ordered it cut into two channels eastward on either side of Huacheng, and the harm grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, on xinyou, the Yellow River swelled and threatened to wash away the walls of Hua Prefecture. Zhu Quanzhong had it split into two channels running east on either side of the city, and the damage only grew worse.

sentences.zh: 李克用擊羅弘信，攻洹水，殺魏兵萬餘，進攻魏州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong attacked Luo Hongxin, assaulted Huanshui, killed over ten thousand Wei troops, and advanced to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong struck Luo Hongxin, stormed Huanshui, killed more than ten thousand Wei soldiers, and pressed on against Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 武安節度使劉建鋒既得志，嗜酒，不親政事。

translations.literal: Liu Jianfeng, military governor of Wu'an, once he had attained his ambitions, became addicted to wine and neglected government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once Liu Jianfeng, military governor of Wu'an, had got what he wanted, he took to drink and stopped tending to affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 長直兵陳贍妻美，建鋒私之。

translations.literal: Chen Shan of the long-duty guard had a beautiful wife whom Jianfeng took for himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shan of the long-duty guard had a beautiful wife, and Jianfeng seduced her.

sentences.zh: 贍袖鐵撾擊殺建鋒；

translations.literal: Shan concealed an iron mace in his sleeve and killed Jianfeng;
translations.idiomatic: Shan hid an iron mace in his sleeve and beat Jianfeng to death;

sentences.zh: 諸將殺贍，迎行軍司馬張佶為留後。

translations.literal: the generals killed Shan and welcomed marching secretary Zhang Ji as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: the other generals killed Shan and installed marching secretary Zhang Ji as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 佶將入府，馬忽踶嚙，傷左髀。

translations.literal: As Ji was about to enter the headquarters, a horse suddenly kicked and bit him, injuring his left thigh.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Ji was entering the headquarters, a horse suddenly kicked and bit him, wounding his left thigh.

sentences.zh: 時馬殷攻邵州未下，佶謝諸將曰：「馬公勇而有謀，寬厚樂善，吾所不及，真乃主也。」

translations.literal: At the time Ma Yin was attacking Shaozhou without success; Ji told the generals: "Lord Ma is brave and resourceful, generous and fond of doing good—I cannot match him. He is truly the man to lead."
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin was then besieging Shaozhou without success. Ji told the generals, "Lord Ma is brave and shrewd, generous and humane—qualities I lack. He is the true leader."

sentences.zh: 乃以牒召之。

translations.literal: He then summoned him by official dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Yin by official dispatch.

sentences.zh: 殷猶豫未行，聽直軍將汝南姚彥章說殷曰：「公與劉龍驤、張司馬，一體人也，今龍驤遇禍，司馬傷髀，天命人望，捨公尚誰屬哉！」

translations.literal: Yin hesitated and did not go; Yao Yanzhang of Runan, a direct-service officer, urged Yin: "You, the Dragon Chariot General Liu, and Secretary Zhang are one body. Now the Dragon Chariot General has met disaster and the Secretary is wounded in the thigh—Heaven's mandate and men's hopes: who else but you could they fall upon!"
translations.idiomatic: Yin hesitated to go. Yao Yanzhang of Runan, an officer of the direct guard, urged him, "You, General Liu the Dragon Chariot, and Secretary Zhang are one and the same. Now the general is dead and the secretary crippled—by Heaven's mandate and the army's wish, who else should take command!"

sentences.zh: 殷乃使親從都指揮使李瓊留攻邵州，逕詣長沙。

translations.literal: Yin then left chief attendant commander Li Qiong to continue the attack on Shaozhou and went straight to Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then left Li Qiong, chief attendant commander, to keep pressing Shaozhou and went straight to Changsha.

sentences.zh: 淮南兵與鎮海兵戰於皇天蕩，鎮海兵不利，楊行密遂圍蘇州。

translations.literal: Huainan and Zhenhai troops fought at Huangtian Dang; Zhenhai troops fared poorly, and Yang Xingmi proceeded to besiege Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huainan and Zhenhai forces clashed at Huangtian Dang. The Zhenhai army got the worse of it, and Yang Xingmi went on to besiege Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐、鍾傳、杜洪畏楊行密之強，皆求援於朱全忠；

translations.literal: Qian Liu, Zhong Chuan, and Du Hong, fearing Yang Xingmi's strength, all sought aid from Zhu Quanzhong;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, Zhong Chuan, and Du Hong, alarmed by Yang Xingmi's power, all appealed to Zhu Quanzhong for help;

sentences.zh: 全忠遣許州刺史朱友恭將兵萬人渡淮，聽以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Zhu Yougong, prefect of Xuzhou, with ten thousand troops across the Huai River, authorizing him to act as he saw fit.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Zhu Yougong, prefect of Xuzhou, with ten thousand men across the Huai, with full discretion to act as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 董昌使人覘錢鏐兵，有言其強盛者輒怒，斬之；

translations.literal: Dong Chang sent men to reconnoiter Qian Liu's army; anyone who reported it strong and flourishing he at once flew into a rage and executed;
translations.idiomatic: Dong Chang sent scouts to watch Qian Liu's army. Anyone who reported that it was strong and well supplied he flew into a rage and killed;

sentences.zh: 言兵疲食盡，則賞之。

translations.literal: those who said the troops were exhausted and provisions gone he rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: anyone who said the troops were weary and food was running out he rewarded.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，袁邠以餘姚降於鏐；

translations.literal: On wuyin, Yuan Bin surrendered Yuyao to Liu;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Yuan Bin surrendered Yuyao to Qian Liu;

sentences.zh: 顧全武、許再思進兵至越州城下。

translations.literal: Gu Quanwu and Xu Zaisi advanced their troops to the walls of Yue Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Quanwu and Xu Zaisi pushed their army to the walls of Yue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 五月，昌出戰而敗，嬰城自守，全武等圍之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Chang came out to fight and was defeated, barricaded himself in the city, and Quanwu and others besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Chang sallied out, was beaten, shut himself inside the city, and Quanwu and the others laid siege.

sentences.zh: 昌始懼，去帝號，復稱節度使。

translations.literal: Chang at last grew afraid, abandoned his imperial title, and resumed calling himself military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Chang finally lost nerve, dropped his imperial title, and styled himself military governor once more.

sentences.zh: 馬殷至長沙，張佶肩輿入府，坐受殷拜謁，已，乃命殷升聽事，以留後讓之，即趨下，帥將吏拜賀，復為行軍司馬，代殷將兵攻邵州。

translations.literal: When Ma Yin reached Changsha, Zhang Ji entered the headquarters in a sedan chair, seated himself and received Yin's bow and salutation; then he had Yin ascend the audience hall, yielded the post of acting governor to him, immediately hurried below, led the officers in bowing congratulations, resumed his post as marching secretary, and took over Yin's troops to attack Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Yin arrived at Changsha, Zhang Ji was carried into headquarters in a sedan chair, sat in place, and received Yin's bow. Then he had Yin ascend the audience hall, surrendered the acting governorship to him, stepped down at once, and with the officers bowed in congratulation before resuming his old post as marching secretary and taking over Yin's troops to continue the attack on Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 癸未，蘇州常熟鎮使陸郢以州城應楊行密，虜刺史成及。

translations.literal: On guiwei, Lu Ying, garrison commander of Changshu in Suzhou, opened the prefectural city to Yang Xingmi and captured prefect Cheng Ji.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Lu Ying, garrison commander of Changshu in Suzhou, turned the prefectural city over to Yang Xingmi and seized the prefect Cheng Ji.

sentences.zh: 行密閱及家所蓄，惟圖書、藥物，賢之，歸，署行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Xingmi inspected what Ji had stored in his household and found only books and medicines; he admired him, let him return, and appointed him marching secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi examined Ji's household stores and found nothing but books and medicines. Impressed, he released him and appointed him marching secretary.

sentences.zh: 及拜且泣曰：「及百口在錢公所。

translations.literal: Ji bowed and wept, saying: "My household of a hundred mouths is in Lord Qian's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Ji bowed and wept, saying, "My household of a hundred souls is in Lord Qian's hands.

sentences.zh: 失蘇州不能死，敢求富貴！

translations.literal: Having lost Suzhou I could not bring myself to die—how dare I seek wealth and honor!
translations.idiomatic: I failed to die when Suzhou was lost—how dare I now seek rank and reward!

sentences.zh: 願以一身易百口之死！」

translations.literal: I beg to exchange my single life for the deaths of my hundred mouths!"
translations.idiomatic: Let my one life pay for the lives of my hundred kin!"

sentences.zh: 引佩刀欲自刺。

translations.literal: He drew his belt knife intending to kill himself.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the dagger at his belt and tried to stab himself.

sentences.zh: 行密遽執其手，止之，館於府捨。

translations.literal: Xingmi swiftly seized his hand and stopped him, lodging him in a guesthouse of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi caught his hand at once and held him back, then housed him in a guest wing of headquarters.

sentences.zh: 其室中亦有兵仗，行密每單衣詣之，與之共飲膳，無所疑。

translations.literal: Weapons were also kept in his rooms, yet Xingmi came to him in simple dress each time, shared food and drink with him, and harbored no suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Though weapons were kept in his quarters, Xingmi visited him each time in plain clothes, ate and drank with him, and never showed mistrust.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐聞蘇州陷，急召顧全武，使趨西陵備行密，全武曰：「越州賊之根本，奈何垂克而棄之！

translations.literal: When Qian Liu heard Suzhou had fallen, he urgently summoned Gu Quanwu and ordered him to hurry to Xiling to guard against Xingmi; Quanwu said: "Yue Prefecture is the rebels' root—how can we abandon it when we are on the verge of taking it!
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Liu learned Suzhou had fallen, he urgently recalled Gu Quanwu and ordered him to rush to Xiling to block Yang Xingmi. Quanwu replied, "Yue Prefecture is the heart of the rebellion—how can we walk away when we are about to take it!

sentences.zh: 請先取越州，後復甦州。」

translations.literal: I beg first to take Yue Prefecture, then recover Suzhou."
translations.idiomatic: Let me seize Yue Prefecture first, then win back Suzhou."

sentences.zh: 鏐從之。

translations.literal: Liu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu agreed.

sentences.zh: 淮南將朱延壽奄至蘄州，圍其城。

translations.literal: Huainan general Zhu Yanshou suddenly reached Qizhou and besieged the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan general Zhu Yanshou suddenly appeared at Qizhou and surrounded the city.

sentences.zh: 大將賈公鐸方獵，不得還，伏兵林中，命勇士二人衣羊皮夜入延壽所掠羊群，潛入城，約夜半開門舉火為應，復衣皮返命。

translations.literal: Great general Jia Gongduo was out hunting and could not return; he hid troops in the forest, ordered two brave men to dress in sheepskin at night, enter among the sheep Yanshou had plundered, slip into the city, arrange to open the gate and raise fire as a signal at midnight, then put on the skins again and return with the report.
translations.idiomatic: The great general Jia Gongduo was out hunting and could not get back. He hid soldiers in the woods and sent two bold men, clad in sheepskins by night, to mingle with the flock Yanshou had seized, slip into the city, and arrange to open the gate and raise a fire at midnight as the signal; then, still in sheepskin, they returned with word.

sentences.zh: 公鐸如期引兵至城南，門中火舉，力戰，突圍而入。

translations.literal: Gongduo led his troops to the south gate on schedule; fire rose at the gate, and fighting fiercely he burst through the encirclement and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Gongduo brought his troops to the south gate on time. Fire flared at the gate; fighting hard, he broke through the ring and entered the city.

sentences.zh: 延壽驚曰：「吾常恐其潰圍而出，反潰圍而入，如此，城安可猝拔！」

translations.literal: Yanshou cried out in alarm: "I always feared they would break out—instead they broke in! With things like this, how can the city be taken quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou exclaimed in alarm, "I kept worrying they would break out—instead they broke in! At this rate, how can the city be taken in a hurry!"

sentences.zh: 乃白行密，求軍中與公鐸有舊者持誓書金帛往說之，許以婚。

translations.literal: He reported to Xingmi, requesting someone in the army who had old ties with Gongduo to go with sworn oaths, gold, and silk to persuade him, promising marriage.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to Xingmi and asked for someone in the army who had old ties with Gongduo to go with sworn pledges, gold, and silk to win him over, offering a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 壽州團練副使柴再用請行，臨城與語，為陳利害。

translations.literal: Chai Zaiyong, deputy training commissioner of Shouzhou, volunteered; he spoke with Gongduo from beneath the walls and set out the advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Zaiyong, deputy training commissioner of Shouzhou, offered to go. He talked with Gongduo from below the walls and laid out the stakes.

sentences.zh: 數日，公鐸及刺史馮敬章請降。

translations.literal: After several days, Gongduo and prefect Feng Jingzhang requested to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days, Gongduo and the prefect Feng Jingzhang asked to surrender.

sentences.zh: 以敬章為左都押牙，公鐸為右監門衛將軍。

translations.literal: Jingzhang was made Left Chief Adjutant; Gongduo was made Right Gate Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jingzhang was made Left Chief Adjutant, and Gongduo Right Gate Guard general.

sentences.zh: 延壽進拔光州，殺刺吏劉存。

translations.literal: Yanshou proceeded to capture Guang Prefecture and killed prefect Liu Cun.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou went on to take Guang Prefecture and killed its prefect, Liu Cun.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，上遣中使詣梓州和解兩川，王建雖奉詔還成都，然猶連兵未解。

translations.literal: On bingxu, the emperor sent a palace envoy to Zizhou to reconcile the two Sichuan circuits; Wang Jian, though he obeyed the edict and returned to Chengdu, still kept his troops linked in unresolved hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, the emperor dispatched a palace envoy to Zizhou to mediate between the two Sichuan circuits. Wang Jian obeyed the edict and returned to Chengdu, but his armies remained in the field and the fighting did not stop.

sentences.zh: 崔昭緯復求救於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Cui Zhaowei again sought rescue from Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei once again appealed to Zhu Quanzhong for help.

sentences.zh: 戊子，遣中使賜昭緯死，行至荊南，追及，斬之，中外咸以為快。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the emperor dispatched a palace envoy to grant Zhaowei death; when the envoy reached Jingnan, he was overtaken and beheaded; inside and outside the court all deemed it satisfying.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, the emperor sent a palace envoy to order Zhaowei's death. The envoy caught up with him in Jingnan and beheaded him. Throughout court and country alike, people felt justice had been done.

sentences.zh: 荊南節度使成汭與其將許存溯江略地，盡取濱江州縣。

translations.literal: Cheng Ru, military governor of Jingnan, and his general Xu Cun sailed upstream to seize territory, taking all the prefectures and counties along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ru, military governor of Jingnan, and his general Xu Cun pushed upriver to expand their holdings, seizing every prefecture and county along the banks.

sentences.zh: 武泰節度使王建肇棄黔州，收餘眾保豐都。

translations.literal: Wang Jianzhao, military governor of Wutai, abandoned Qian Prefecture, gathered his remaining forces and held Fengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianzhao, military governor of Wutai, gave up Qian Prefecture, rallied his survivors, and held Fengdu.

sentences.zh: 存又引兵西取諭、涪二州，汭以其將趙武為黔中留後，存為萬州刺史。

translations.literal: Cun then led troops west to take Yu and Fu prefectures; Ru made his general Zhao Wu acting governor of Qianzhong and Cun prefect of Wanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Cun then marched west and took Yu and Fu prefectures. Cheng Ru appointed his general Zhao Wu acting governor of Qianzhong and made Cun prefect of Wanzhou.

sentences.zh: 汭知存不得志，使人詗之，曰：「存不治州事，日出蹴鞠。」

translations.literal: Ru knew Cun was discontent; he sent someone to spy, who reported: "Cun does not administer the prefectural affairs—each day he goes out playing cuju."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ru knew Cun was unhappy. He sent a spy who reported, "Cun ignores the prefectural business and goes out every day to play cuju."

sentences.zh: 汭曰：「存將逃，先勻足力也。」

translations.literal: Ru said: "Cun is about to flee—he is first limbering his legs."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ru said, "Cun means to run—he is limbering up first."

sentences.zh: 遣兵襲之，存棄城走；

translations.literal: He sent troops to surprise him; Cun abandoned the city and fled;
translations.idiomatic: He sent troops to surprise him. Cun abandoned the city and fled;

sentences.zh: 其眾稍稍歸之，屯於茅壩。

translations.literal: his troops gradually rejoined him, and he encamped at Maoba.
translations.idiomatic: his men slowly gathered back to him, and he made camp at Maoba.

sentences.zh: 趙武數攻豐都，王建肇不能守，與存皆降於王建，建忌存勇略，欲殺之，掌書記高燭曰：「公方總攬英雄以圖霸業，彼窮來歸我，奈何殺之！」

translations.literal: Zhao Wu repeatedly attacked Fengdu; Wang Jianzhao could not hold out; both he and Cun surrendered to Wang Jian; Jian, envious of Cun's courage and strategy, wished to kill him; chief secretary Gao Zhu said: "Your Lordship is now gathering heroes to pursue dominion—he came to us in desperation; how can you kill him!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Wu attacked Fengdu again and again until Wang Jianzhao could no longer hold out. Both he and Xu Cun submitted to Wang Jian. Jian, wary of Cun's bravery and skill, wanted him killed. Chief secretary Gao Zhu said, "Your Lordship is rallying heroes to build an empire. This man came to us in defeat—why kill him!"

sentences.zh: 建使戍蜀州，陰使知蜀州王宗綰察之。

translations.literal: Jian sent him to garrison Shuzhou and secretly had Shuzhou commissioner Wang Zongkan watch him.
translations.idiomatic: Jian posted him at Shuzhou and secretly ordered Wang Zongkan, commissioner of Shuzhou, to keep watch on him.

sentences.zh: 宗綰密言存忠勇廉厚，有良將才，建乃捨之，更其姓名臼王宗播，而宗綰竟不使宗播知其免己也。

translations.literal: Zongkan secretly reported that Cun was loyal, brave, honest, and generous, with the talents of a fine general; Jian then spared him, changed his surname and given name to Wang Zongbo, and Zongkan never let Zongbo know he had saved his life.
translations.idiomatic: Zongkan secretly reported that Cun was loyal, brave, upright, and generous—a born commander. Jian spared him, changed his name to Wang Zongbo, and Zongkan never told Zongbo that he had saved him.

sentences.zh: 宗播元從也目官柳修業，每勸宗播慎靜以免禍。

translations.literal: Liu Xiuye, a clerk in Zongbo's original retinue, constantly urged Zongbo to be cautious and calm to avoid disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiuye, a clerk who had followed Zongbo from the start, always urged him to stay careful and quiet so as to avoid trouble.

sentences.zh: 其後宗播為建將，遇強敵諸將所憚者，以身先之。

translations.literal: Later, as Jian's general, whenever they encountered a strong foe that other generals feared, Zongbo took the lead himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later, serving Wang Jian as a general, whenever the army faced a formidable enemy that others shrank from, Zongbo led from the front.

sentences.zh: 及有功，輒稱病，不自伐，由是得以功名終。

translations.literal: When he had merit he always claimed illness and did not boast of himself; thereby he was able to bring his career of fame and achievement to a peaceful end.
translations.idiomatic: After each success he would plead illness and never boast, and so lived out his days in honor and safety.

sentences.zh: 甲午，夜，顧全武急攻越州，乙未旦，克其外郭，董昌猶據牙城拒之。

translations.literal: On jiawu, at night, Gu Quanwu pressed the attack on Yue Prefecture; at dawn on yiwei he captured the outer city; Dong Chang still held the headquarters compound and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, by night, Gu Quanwu stormed Yue Prefecture. At dawn on yiwei he took the outer city, but Dong Chang still held the headquarters compound and fought on.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，鏐遣昌故將駱團紿昌云：「奉詔，令大王致仕歸臨安。」

translations.literal: On wuxu, Liu sent Dong Chang's former general Luo Tuan to deceive Chang, saying: "By imperial edict, the Great King is ordered to retire and return to Lin'an."
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Qian Liu sent Dong Chang's old general Luo Tuan to trick him, saying, "By imperial decree, the Great King is to retire and return to Lin'an."

sentences.zh: 昌乃送牌印，出居清道坊。

translations.literal: Chang then surrendered his seals and credentials and went out to reside on Qingdao Lane.
translations.idiomatic: Chang handed over his seals and insignia and moved out to Qingdao Lane.

sentences.zh: 己亥，全武遣武勇都監使吳璋以舟載昌如杭州，至小江南，斬之，並其家三百餘人，宰相李邈、蔣瑰以下百餘人。

translations.literal: On jihai, Quanwu sent Wu Yong deputy commissioner Wu Zhang in a boat to convey Chang toward Hangzhou; at Xiaojiangnan he beheaded him, along with over three hundred members of his household and over a hundred others including chief ministers Li Miao and Jiang Gui and their retinues.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai, Quanwu sent Wu Zhang, deputy commissioner of the Wu Yong corps, to carry Chang by boat toward Hangzhou. At Xiaojiangnan he executed him, together with more than three hundred of his household and more than a hundred others, including the chief ministers Li Miao and Jiang Gui and their followers.

sentences.zh: 昌在圍城中，貪吝益甚，口率民間錢帛，減戰士糧。

translations.literal: While Chang was besieged in the city, his greed and stinginess grew ever worse; he constantly levied money and silk from the populace and cut the soldiers' rations.
translations.idiomatic: During the siege, Dong Chang grew ever greedier and meaner. He squeezed the townspeople for cash and cloth and slashed the soldiers' rations.

sentences.zh: 及城破，庫有金帛雜貨五百間，倉有糧三百萬斛。

translations.literal: When the city fell, the treasury held gold, silk, and assorted goods filling five hundred bays, and the granaries held three million hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: When the city finally fell, the treasury held gold, silk, and assorted goods in five hundred storehouse bays, and the granaries held three million hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐傳昌首於京師，散金帛以賞將士，開倉以振貧乏。

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent Dong Chang's head to the capital, distributed gold and silk to reward the officers and soldiers, and opened the granaries to relieve the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent Dong Chang's head to the capital, distributed gold and silk to reward his troops, and opened the granaries to aid the destitute.

sentences.zh: 李克用攻魏博，侵掠遍六州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong attacked Weibo and raided across all six prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong attacked Weibo and carried his raids through all six prefectures.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠召葛從周於鄆州，使將兵營洹水以救魏博，留龐師古攻鄆州，六月，克用引兵擊從周，汴人多鑿坎於陳前，戰方酣，克用之子鐵林指揮使落落馬遇坎而躓，汴人生擒之；

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong summoned Ge Congzhou at Yun Prefecture, had him lead troops to encamp on the Huan River to rescue Weibo, and left Pang Shigu to press the attack on Yun Prefecture. In the sixth month Li Keyong led his army against Congzhou. The Bian troops dug many pits in front of their battle line; as the fighting grew fierce, Li Keyong's son Luoluo, commander of the Iron Forest Corps, stumbled when his horse hit a pit, and the Bian troops captured him alive;
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong recalled Ge Congzhou to Yun Prefecture and sent him to encamp on the Huan River and relieve Weibo, leaving Pang Shigu to continue the siege of Yun. In the sixth month Li Keyong marched against Congzhou. The Bian army dug pits across the front of its line; in the heat of battle Li Keyong's son Luoluo, commander of the Iron Forest Corps, was thrown when his horse struck a pit, and Bian soldiers took him alive;

sentences.zh: 克用自往救之。

translations.literal: Keyong went in person to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong rode forward to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 馬亦躓，幾為汴人所獲；

translations.literal: His horse also stumbled, and he was nearly taken by the Bian troops;
translations.idiomatic: His own horse stumbled too, and he was nearly captured by the Bian troops;

sentences.zh: 克用顧射汴將一人，斃之，乃得免。

translations.literal: Keyong turned and shot one Bian general, killing him, and only then escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong wheeled about, shot down a Bian general, and only then got away.

sentences.zh: 克用請修好以贖落落，全忠不許，以與羅弘信，使殺之。

translations.literal: Keyong asked to restore friendly relations in order to ransom Luoluo; Quanzhong refused and handed him to Luo Hongxin, who had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong offered to renew peace in exchange for Luoluo's release, but Quanzhong refused and turned the captive over to Luo Hongxin, who had him killed.

sentences.zh: 克用引軍還。

translations.literal: Keyong withdrew his army.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong withdrew his army.

sentences.zh: 葛從周自洹水引兵濟河，屯於楊劉，復擊鄆，及兗、鄆、河東之兵戰於故樂亭，破之，兗、鄆屬城皆為汴人所據，屢求救於李克用，克用發兵赴之，為羅弘信所拒，不得前，兗、鄆由是不振。

translations.literal: Ge Congzhou led his troops from the Huan River across the Yellow River, encamped at Yangliu, and again struck at Yun. He joined Yan, Yun, and Hedong forces in battle at the old Yue Pavilion and defeated them. All subordinate cities of Yan and Yun fell to the Bian troops. They repeatedly begged Li Keyong for help; Keyong sent troops to their aid, but Luo Hongxin blocked them and they could not advance, and Yan and Yun therefore never recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Congzhou crossed the Yellow River from the Huan River, encamped at Yangliu, and renewed the attack on Yun. At the old Yue Pavilion he joined battle with the Yan, Yun, and Hedong armies and routed them. Every dependent city in Yan and Yun fell to the Bian forces. They pleaded repeatedly to Li Keyong for relief; Keyong sent troops, but Luo Hongxin barred their way and they could not get through, and Yan and Yun never recovered their strength.

sentences.zh: 初，李克用屯渭北，李茂貞、韓建憚之，事朝廷禮甚恭。

translations.literal: At first, while Li Keyong was encamped north of the Wei River, Li Maozhen and Han Jian feared him and treated the court with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Li Keyong held the north bank of the Wei River, Li Maozhen and Han Jian feared him and were scrupulously deferential toward the court.

sentences.zh: 克用去，二鎮貢獻漸疏，表章驕慢，上自石門還，於神策兩軍之外，更置軍聖、捧宸、保寧、宣化等軍，選補數萬人，使諸王將之；

translations.literal: After Keyong departed, the two circuits slackened their tribute and their memorials grew arrogant and insolent. When the emperor returned from Shimen, outside the two Shence Armies he additionally established the Junsheng, Pengchen, Baoning, Xuanhua, and other armies, selected and filled them with tens of thousands of men, and had the imperial princes command them;
translations.idiomatic: Once Keyong was gone, the two circuits grew stingy with tribute and their memorials turned proud and disrespectful. After the emperor returned from Shimen, he raised new armies—the Junsheng, Pengchen, Baoning, Xuanhua, and others—outside the two Shence corps, enrolled tens of thousands of men, and put the imperial princes in command;

sentences.zh: 嗣延王戒丕、嗣賈王嗣周又自募麾下數千人。

translations.literal: The Heir Prince of Yan, Jiepi, and the Heir Prince of He, Sizhou, each also recruited several thousand men from their personal followings.
translations.idiomatic: The Heir Prince of Yan, Jiepi, and the Heir Prince of He, Sizhou, each raised several thousand men from their own households as well.

sentences.zh: 茂貞以為欲討己；

translations.literal: Maozhen believed they intended to attack him;
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen took this as preparation for an attack on himself;

sentences.zh: 語多怨望，嫌隙日構。

translations.literal: his words were full of resentment, and mutual suspicion grew day by day.
translations.idiomatic: his complaints grew bitter, and mutual suspicion deepened by the day.

sentences.zh: 茂貞亦勒兵揚言欲詣闕訟冤；

translations.literal: Maozhen also mobilized his troops and publicly declared that he would go to the palace to plead his grievances;
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen also mustered his troops and announced that he would march to the capital to plead his case;

sentences.zh: 京師士民爭亡匿山谷。

translations.literal: the gentry and common people of the capital scrambled to flee and hide in the hills.
translations.idiomatic: men and women of the capital fled in panic to hide in the hills.

sentences.zh: 上命通王滋及嗣周、戒丕分將諸軍以衛近畿，戒丕屯三橋。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Prince Zi and Sizhou and Jiepi to divide command of the armies to guard the capital region; Jiepi encamped at Sanqiao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Zi, together with Sizhou and Jiepi, to divide command of the armies and guard the approaches to the capital; Jiepi took position at Sanqiao.

sentences.zh: 茂貞遂表言「延王無故稱兵討臣，臣今勒兵入朝請罪。」

translations.literal: Maozhen then submitted a memorial stating, "The Yan Prince has raised troops without cause to attack me; I now lead my army to the court to submit to judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen then memorialized the throne: "The Yan Prince has mobilized without cause to attack me; I now lead my army to the capital to accept punishment."

sentences.zh: 上遽遣使告急於河東。

translations.literal: The emperor hastily sent envoys to Hedong to plead for aid.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at once dispatched envoys to Hedong to beg for help.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，茂貞引兵逼京畿，覃王與戰於婁館，官軍敗績。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Maozhen led his troops to press the capital region; the Tan Prince fought him at Lou Pavilion, and the imperial army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Maozhen advanced on the capital approaches. The Tan Prince met him at Lou Pavilion, and the imperial army was routed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，茂貞進逼京師。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Maozhen pressed closer on the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Maozhen closed in on the capital.

sentences.zh: 延王戒丕曰：「今關中籓鎮無可依者，不若自鄜州濟河，幸太原，臣請先往告之。」

translations.literal: The Yan Prince Jiepi said, "At present no frontier command in Guanzhong can be relied upon. It would be better to cross the river from Fu Prefecture and go to Taiyuan; your servant asks to go ahead and announce your coming."
translations.idiomatic: The Yan Prince Jiepi said, "There is no loyal command left in Guanzhong to shelter us. Better to cross the river from Fu Prefecture and seek refuge at Taiyuan; let me go ahead and announce your coming."

sentences.zh: 辛卯，詔幸鄜州；

translations.literal: On xinmao an edict was issued for the emperor to proceed to Fu Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the court ordered the emperor's progress to Fu Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，上出至渭北；

translations.literal: on renchen the emperor went out as far as the north bank of the Wei River;
translations.idiomatic: on renchen the emperor left the capital and reached the north bank of the Wei;

sentences.zh: 韓建遣其子從允奉表請幸華州，上不許，以建為亦畿都指揮、安撫制置及開通四面道路、催促諸道綱運等使。

translations.literal: Han Jian sent his son Congyun with a memorial inviting the emperor to visit Hua Prefecture; the emperor did not agree, but appointed Jian commander of the capital region, commissioner for pacification and disposition, and commissioner for opening roads on all sides and urging tribute transport from every circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian sent his son Congyun with a memorial inviting the emperor to Hua Prefecture. The emperor refused, but appointed Jian commander of the capital region, commissioner for pacification and disposition, and commissioner for opening roads on all sides and pressing the circuits for tribute shipments.

sentences.zh: 而建奉表相繼，上及從官亦憚遠去，癸己，至富平，遣宣徽使元公訊召建，面議去留。

translations.literal: Yet Jian's memorials followed one after another, and the emperor and his attendants also feared going far away. On guisi they reached Fuping and sent Privy Envoy Yuan Gongxun to summon Jian for a face-to-face discussion of whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's invitations kept coming, and the emperor and his entourage shrank from going farther afield. On guisi they reached Fuping and sent Privy Envoy Yuan Gongxun to summon Jian for a personal discussion of what to do next.

sentences.zh: 甲午，建詣富平見上，頓首涕泣言：「方今籓臣跋扈者，非止茂貞。

translations.literal: On jiawu, Jian came to Fuping to see the emperor, bowed his head to the ground, and said through tears, "At present the insolent frontier lords are not limited to Maozhen alone.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu Jian came to Fuping to see the emperor, kowtowed, and said through tears, "The overmighty frontier lords are not Maozhen alone.

sentences.zh: 陛下若去宗廟園陵，遠巡邊鄙，臣恐車駕濟河，無復還期。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty leaves the ancestral temples and imperial tombs and makes a distant tour of the borderlands, I fear that once the imperial carriage crosses the river there will be no day of return.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty abandons the ancestral temples and tombs and wanders far into the borderlands, I fear that once the imperial carriage crosses the river it will never return.

sentences.zh: 今華州兵力雖微，控帶關輔，亦足自固。

translations.literal: Although Hua Prefecture's military strength is slight, it commands the Guanzhong region and is sufficient for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Prefecture's forces are few, but it holds the gateway to Guanzhong and is strong enough to defend itself.

sentences.zh: 臣積聚訓厲，十五年矣，西距長安不遠，願陛下臨之，以圖興復。」

translations.literal: Your servant has gathered stores and trained troops for fifteen years; it lies not far west of Chang'an. I beg Your Majesty to come there and plan restoration."
translations.idiomatic: I have gathered supplies and drilled troops for fifteen years, and it lies only a short march west of Chang'an. I beg Your Majesty to make it your seat and plan the restoration from there."

sentences.zh: 上乃從之。

translations.literal: The emperor then agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted.

sentences.zh: 乙未，宿下邽；

translations.literal: On yiwei he lodged at Xia_gui;
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei he spent the night at Xia_gui;

sentences.zh: 丙申，至華州，以府署為行宮；

translations.literal: on bingshen he reached Hua Prefecture and made the prefectural offices his traveling palace;
translations.idiomatic: on bingshen he reached Hua Prefecture and turned the prefectural offices into his temporary palace;

sentences.zh: 建視事於龍興寺。

translations.literal: Jian conducted affairs at Longxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Jian conducted government business from Longxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 茂貞遂入長安，自中和以來所葺宮室、市肆，燔燒俱盡。

translations.literal: Maozhen then entered Chang'an; the palace buildings and market stalls repaired since the Zhonghe era were burned entirely away.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhen then entered Chang'an and burned to the ground every palace building and market stall rebuilt since the Zhonghe era.

sentences.zh: 乙己，以中書侍郎、同平章事崔胤同平章事，充武安節棄使。

translations.literal: On yisi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councilor Cui Yin was retained as Co-Grand Councilor and appointed Military Governor of Wu'an.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councilor Cui Yin was kept on as grand councilor and sent out as Military Governor of Wu'an.

sentences.zh: 上以胤，崔昭緯之黨也，故出之。

translations.literal: The emperor considered Yin a partisan of Cui Zhaowei and therefore sent him out.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor regarded Yin as a follower of Cui Zhaowei and therefore posted him away from court.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以翰林學士承旨、尚書左丞陸扆為戶部侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On bingwu, Academician Expositor and Chief of the Left Department of the Ministry of Works Lu Yi was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Co-Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Academician Expositor and Left Vice Minister of Works Lu Yi was appointed Vice Director of Revenue and Co-Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 扆，陝人也。

translations.literal: Yi was a native of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was a native of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 水部郎中何迎表薦國子《毛詩》博士襄陽朱朴，才如謝安，道士許巖士亦薦朴有經濟才。

translations.literal: Director of Waterways He Ying memorialized recommending Zhu Pu of Xiangyang, Doctor of the Mao Classic at the Imperial Academy, as a talent equal to Xie An; the Daoist priest Xu Yanshi also recommended Pu as having talent for statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: He Ying, Director of the Waterways Bureau, memorialized recommending Zhu Pu of Xiangyang, Imperial Academy doctor of the Mao Classic, as a man of Xie An's caliber; the Daoist Xu Yanshi also praised Pu as a statesman.

sentences.zh: 上連日召對，朴有口辯，上悅之，曰：「朕雖非太宗，得卿如魏徵矣。」

translations.literal: The emperor summoned him for audience day after day. Pu was eloquent in debate, and the emperor was pleased, saying, "Although I am no Taizong, in gaining you I have found my Wei Zheng."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him to audience day after day. Pu was quick and persuasive, and the emperor was delighted. "I may not be Taizong," he said, "but in you I have found my Wei Zheng."

sentences.zh: 賜以金帛，並賜何迎。

translations.literal: He bestowed gold and silk, and also rewarded He Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He rewarded them with gold and silk, and He Ying received a gift as well.

sentences.zh: 以徐彥若為大明宮留守，兼京畿安撫制置等使。

translations.literal: Xu Yanruo was made Keeper of the Daming Palace and concurrently commissioner for pacification and disposition of the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yanruo was appointed Keeper of the Daming Palace and commissioner for pacifying and administering the capital region.

sentences.zh: 楊行密表請上遷都江淮，王建請上幸成都。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi memorialized asking that the emperor move the capital to the Jianghuai region; Wang Jian asked that the emperor visit Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi memorialized urging the emperor to move the capital to the Jianghuai region; Wang Jian invited him to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 宰相畏韓建，不敢專決政事。

translations.literal: The chief ministers feared Han Jian and did not dare decide state affairs on their own.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers feared Han Jian and no longer dared decide affairs on their own.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙辰，詔建關議朝政；

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingchen, an edict ordered Jian to join in deliberations on court affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingchen, the emperor ordered Han Jian to take part in deliberations on court affairs;

sentences.zh: 建上表固辭，乃止。

translations.literal: Jian submitted a memorial firmly declining, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Jian memorialized a firm refusal, and the order was withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 韓建移檄諸道，令共輸資糧詣行在。

translations.literal: Han Jian issued a proclamation to all circuits ordering them jointly to send supplies and grain to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian issued a circular to every circuit ordering them to send supplies and grain to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 李克用聞之，歎曰：「去歲從余言，豈有今日之患！」

translations.literal: When Li Keyong heard of this he sighed and said, "Had he followed my counsel last year, how could there be today's calamity!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Keyong heard this he sighed and said, "Had he taken my advice last year, he would never be in today's plight!"

sentences.zh: 又曰：「韓建天下癡物，為賊臣弱帝室，是不為李茂貞所擒，則為朱全忠所虜耳！」

translations.literal: He also said, "Han Jian is the greatest fool under heaven. By weakening the imperial house for treacherous ministers, if he is not seized by Li Maozhen he will be captured by Zhu Quanzhong!"
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Han Jian is the greatest fool alive. By weakening the throne for treacherous ministers, he will end up in Li Maozhen's hands if not Zhu Quanzhong's!"

sentences.zh: 因奏將與鄰道發兵入援。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that he would mobilize neighboring circuits and send troops to the emperor's aid.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that he would raise troops from neighboring circuits and march to the emperor's relief.

sentences.zh: 加錢鏐兼中書令。

translations.literal: Qian Liu was additionally appointed Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以王建為鳳翔西面行營招討使。

translations.literal: On guichou, Wang Jian was made Commander-in-Chief of the Western Fengxiang Campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Wang Jian was appointed commander-in-chief of the western Fengxiang campaign.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以門下侍郎、同平章事王摶同平章事，充威勝節度使。

translations.literal: On jiayin, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councilor Wang Tuan was retained as Co-Grand Councilor and appointed Military Governor of Weisheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Grand Councilor Wang Tuan was kept on as grand councilor and sent out as Military Governor of Weisheng.

sentences.zh: 上憤天下之亂，思得奇傑之士不次用之。

translations.literal: The emperor resented the chaos under heaven and wished to obtain extraordinary men of talent and employ them out of turn.
translations.idiomatic: Angered by the chaos engulfing the empire, the emperor longed for exceptional talent and was ready to promote men out of turn.

sentences.zh: 國子博士朱朴自言：「得為宰相，月餘可致太平。」

translations.literal: Imperial Academy Doctor Zhu Pu declared of himself, "If I am made chief minister, within a little over a month I can bring about great peace."
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Pu, a doctor at the Imperial Academy, declared, "Make me chief minister, and within a month I will restore peace."

sentences.zh: 上以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor believed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，以朴為左諫議大夫、同平章事。

translations.literal: On yichou, Pu was made Left Remonstrance Councilor and Co-Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Pu was appointed Left Remonstrance Councilor and Co-Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 朴為人庸鄙迂僻，無它長。

translations.literal: Pu as a man was vulgar, base, and narrow-minded, with no other strengths.
translations.idiomatic: Pu was a vulgar, narrow-minded man with no other gifts.

sentences.zh: 製出，中外大驚。

translations.literal: When the appointment was issued, court and country were greatly shocked.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was announced, court and country were stunned.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，加韓建兼中書令。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Han Jian was additionally appointed Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Han Jian was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚辰，升福建為威武軍，以觀察使王潮節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on gengchen, Fujian was elevated to the Weiwu Army, and Observation Commissioner Wang Chao was made its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on gengchen, Fujian was elevated to the Weiwu Army command, and Observation Commissioner Wang Chao was made its military governor.

sentences.zh: 以湖南留後馬殷判湖南軍府事。

translations.literal: Ma Yin, acting commissioner of Hunan, was ordered to administer the military government of Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yin, acting commissioner of Hunan, was put in charge of the Hunan military government.

sentences.zh: 殷以高郁為謀主。

translations.literal: Yin took Gao Yu as his chief strategist.
translations.idiomatic: Yin made Gao Yu his chief strategist.

sentences.zh: 郁，揚州人也。

translations.literal: Yu was a native of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was a native of Yang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 殷畏楊行密、成汭之強，議以金帛結之，高郁曰：「成汭不足畏也，行密公之仇。

translations.literal: Yin feared the strength of Yang Xingmi and Cheng Ru and proposed winning them with gold and silk. Gao Yu said, "Cheng Ru is not worth fearing, but Xingmi is our lord's enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Yin feared the power of Yang Xingmi and Cheng Ru and proposed buying their friendship with gold and silk. Gao Yu said, "Cheng Ru is no threat, but Xingmi is our master's enemy.

sentences.zh: 雖以萬金賂之，安肯為吾援乎！

translations.literal: Even if we bribed him with ten thousand in gold, how would he be willing to aid us!
translations.idiomatic: Even ten thousand in gold would not make him our ally!

sentences.zh: 不若上奉天子，下撫士民，訓卒厲兵，以修霸業，則誰與為敵矣。」

translations.literal: Better to serve the Son of Heaven above and soothe soldiers and people below, drill the troops and sharpen the weapons, and build a hegemonic enterprise—then who would be our enemy?"
translations.idiomatic: Better to honor the Son of Heaven, win over soldiers and people, drill the ranks and sharpen the blades, and build a power of our own—then who could stand against us?"

sentences.zh: 殷從之。

translations.literal: Yin followed his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Yin took his advice.

sentences.zh: 崔胤出鎮湖南，韓建之志也。

translations.literal: Cui Yin's assignment as military governor of Hunan was Han Jian's doing.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yin's posting to Hunan was Han Jian's work.

sentences.zh: 胤密求援於朱全忠，且教之營東都宮闕，表迎車駕，且全忠與河南尹張全義表請上廷都洛陽，全忠仍請以兵二萬迎車駕，且言崔胤忠臣，不宜出外。

translations.literal: Yin secretly sought aid from Zhu Quanzhong and also instructed him to repair the eastern capital's palace halls, memorialize to welcome the imperial carriage, and join Henan Prefect Zhang Quanyi in asking that the emperor establish his court at Luoyang. Quanzhong further asked to bring twenty thousand troops to welcome the imperial carriage and stated that Cui Yin was a loyal minister who should not be sent outside.
translations.idiomatic: Yin secretly appealed to Zhu Quanzhong and urged him to restore the eastern capital's palaces and memorialized inviting the emperor back. Quanzhong and Henan Prefect Zhang Quanyi jointly asked that the court be re-established at Luoyang; Quanzhong also offered twenty thousand troops to escort the emperor and argued that the loyal Cui Yin should not be banished from court.

sentences.zh: 韓建懼，復奏召胤為相，遣使諭全忠以且宜安靜，全忠乃止。

translations.literal: Han Jian was afraid and again memorialized to recall Yin as chief minister; he sent envoys to tell Quanzhong to keep quiet for the time being, and Quanzhong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian was alarmed and memorialized to recall Yin as chief minister; he sent envoys telling Quanzhong to hold his hand for now, and Quanzhong desisted.

sentences.zh: 乙未，復以胤為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Yin was again made Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Yin was restored as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎崔遠同平章事。

translations.literal: Academician Expositor and Vice Director of the Ministry of War Cui Yuan was made Co-Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: Academician Expositor and Vice Director of War Cui Yuan was appointed Co-Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 遠，珙弟璵之孫也。

translations.literal: Yuan was the grandson of Cui Yu, younger brother of Cui Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was the grandson of Cui Yu, younger brother of Cui Gong.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，貶中書侍郎、同平章事陸扆為硤州刺史。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councilor Lu Yi was demoted to Prefect of Xia Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Vice Director of the Secretariat and Co-Grand Councilor Lu Yi was demoted to prefect of Xia Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 崔胤恨扆代己，誣扆，雲黨於李茂貞而貶之。

translations.literal: Cui Yin resented Yi for replacing him, slandered him, and said he was a partisan of Li Maozhen, and had him demoted.
